title: The Queen of Air and Darkness
summary: The heroes chase Varga the Hutt to Cloud City on Bespin, where the Hutt is in deep hiding. Their only lead is the Cloud City Sabacc Tournament — an Imperial paymaster (Lt. Arandis) is making a transfer to one of Varga's proxies at the table. Identify the proxy, trace her back to Varga's hideout, kill the Hutt and recover the courier implant locked in his skull (the only key to the encrypted account). The op ends in a hangar showdown for the Glorious Chariot, an orbital battle over the slave ship The Indemnity, and a moral choice that defines the party. Fallback rendezvous: Maz's castle on Takodana, where Varth uses the recovered implant to unlock the account and pay the crew.

marks.label: Cloud City Welcome
marks.desc: Arrive on Bespin and establish your cover among the high-rollers and hustlers. The Wall of Silence is the city's first message to you — push past it.

marks.label: The Industrial Connection
marks.desc: Fyren and Krygg's Ugnaught labor cooperative is one alliance away from running Bespin's industrial floor against Varga — or with you as its founding partner.

paths.label: Broker the alliance
paths.desc: You shifted who answers to whom on Bespin's industrial floor. The Ugnaught Parliament now runs guild ops to your tempo. Fyren and Krygg owe you. So does the foreman over in Refinery Nine. So do the dockmasters on Platform Twelve.

paths.label: Found the partnership
paths.desc: This is the first lasting relationship that exists because of your hand. Whatever the crew builds later — pirate fleet, rebel cell, sanctuary network — Bespin's Ugnaught Alliance is its first stone. Your name is on the founding document.

marks.label: The Refinery Rumble
marks.desc: Strike Refinery 13. The Imperial Tibanna line, the Indemnity manifest, or the workers' shift — what you break decides what survives.

paths.label: Hit the refinery clean
paths.desc: The Imperial Tibanna pipeline through Refinery 13 is gone. The Empire loses a weapons-grade gas vector for years. You don't get those back without building them again from rock — and the rock isn't on Bespin.

paths.label: Read the manifest
paths.desc: The Indemnity exists. Three hundred eighty-four souls. Sixty-one children. Bound for Vel Shara on the next outbound rotation. You have a name and a number now — and the slave-circuit boarding band the ship answers to.

paths.label: Break the line for the workers
paths.desc: The pipeline broke and the forced-labor rotation broke with it. The crew that comes back to the lower decks tomorrow doesn't come back to the same shift. Krygg's people will sing your name in the Works for years.

marks.label: The Contact
marks.desc: Identify Lt. Arandis, the Imperial paymaster, and the Hutt's proxy he's transferring to. Not everyone at the table is who they seem.

marks.label: The Game Within the Game
marks.desc: Enter the Sabacc tournament — the only place Varga's people surface in public. Watch the table for the handoff. Survive four days of cards under the comm-jamming pin. (Spans p1 s5 → p2 s4; resolved at the handoff scene.)

marks.label: Trace the Proxy
marks.desc: Read the handoff, lean on the Hapan proxy, and pry Varga's hideout out of her before he gets word and bolts. Recover the 137.12 wafer in the same motion.

marks.label: Hangar Bay Showdown
marks.desc: Fight your way through Varga's hangar as the Glorious Chariot primes for launch. End the Hutt — or end him surgically and walk out with what was inside his skull. (Spans p3 s1 → p3 s3; resolved when Varga falls.)

paths.label: End the Hutt
paths.desc: Varga dies in his own hangar. The Western Reaches loses its central spider. Three sectors of slave ledgers, smuggling routes, and Imperial contracts go up for grabs by morning, and every one of them is going to be claimed by somebody worse or somebody better.

paths.label: End him surgically — recover the implant intact
paths.desc: TC-663's Cybot Galactica Model VII comes out clean. The routing data is yours. The Hutt is the price you paid for the data inside his skull, and you walked out of the hangar with the actual prize — not just a kill, but the key to the encrypted account and the Project Leviathan thread that was inside it the whole time.

marks.label: Into the Clouds
marks.desc: The skirmish over Bespin. Three lives are in your hands at once — Maya's pinned at the slave ship, the Indemnity's three hundred and eighty-four are about to jump under Imperial helm, and the Star Destroyer's pursuit is closing. You can't save all of them.

paths.label: Save Maya
paths.desc: She was about to die alone on the slave ship. You broke off and went for her. The road that opened in Adv2 just took its second step — and the Indemnity made the jump to Vel Shara without her, and without you.

paths.label: Save the Indemnity slaves
paths.desc: Three hundred eighty-four souls. Sixty-one children. The slave ship that was bound for Vel Shara is now a lifeboat, jumped to Takodana under your helm. You broke a slave operation in flight. Maya paid for it.

paths.label: Press the Imperial pursuit
paths.desc: You held the line and turned. You burned three TIEs and bloodied a frigate. The Empire counts the cost in a quarterly report. You count it in the bodies you didn't lose to the chase — and in the two lifeboats you didn't go for.

marks.label: The Moral Ledger
marks.desc: Maz's, Takodana, payout day. Varth opens the encrypted account and asks how you want to be paid. The crew's answer now defines who they are. There's no taking it back.

paths.label: Take the payout, walk clean
paths.desc: You took the credits. You went home. You're alive. That's the whole accounting.

paths.label: Take the payout, accept the patron
paths.desc: You're the crew that killed a Hutt and got paid by an admiral. Doors open in the underworld now. Varth has work, and the work has a shape — Crime Lord road, fully visible, fully chosen.

paths.label: Renegotiate the payout — credits for assets
paths.desc: You don't want all your share in credits. You want a slice of Varga's leftover network — his Iron Ring contacts on Takodana, his Tibanna routes, his courier ring. Varth nods. By the time you leave Maz's, Varga's old fixers are sending courier requests to you, not to a dead Hutt. You are building something new on his bones — your own operation, your own crew, your own rules. (Flavor: an Ascendancy-leaning PC may read this as stepping into Varga's empty chair instead — same path, different framing at the table.)

paths.label: Refuse the payout
paths.desc: You give it back. You give it away to Maya, to Denia, to the Indemnity survivors at Maz's — to anyone who isn't you. You will need to find another way to eat. You walk out of Maz's a different person than the one who walked in.

marks.label: The Crucible
marks.desc: The plan catastrophically fails. Improvise under fire to survive.

scenes.title: The Brick Wall
scenes.readAloud:
The Banshee drops out of hyperspace into the amber light of Bespin. Cloud City rises ahead — four centuries of welded durasteel and gas-stained vanes, the same saucer the Ugnaughts welded together for Lord Ecclessis Figg back in the early centuries of the Old Republic, when the Hutts still owned the Outer Rim outright. The platforms have been resurfaced, the running lights replaced, the upper-tier hotels remodeled twice in living memory; the bones underneath are old. From orbit it reads as a working refinery with a casino bolted on, deliberately unimpressive, the kind of polished-but-not-shining quiet a lucrative place becomes when it has spent a hundred and fifty years ducking the attention of one empire after another. Every ten seconds another atmospheric shuttle lifts off the upper landing tiers and another descends. The pre-tournament traffic the Message to Spacers warned you about is real.

Civilian docking bay 327 is your assigned berth. The approach lane is slow and theatrical — designed to show off the city to anyone with the credits to come this far.

As the *Banshee*'s passive sensors finish the docking sweep, the auxiliary scanner stack flags background traffic on a low slave-circuit band — coded chatter on or near 137.12, source intermittent, obvious origin a bulk hauler in low orbit. Varth, dry: "Slave-circuit chatter on 137.12. The Empire is talking to a slave ship and trying to hide that they are doing it. Note the band. We may need it."
scenes.gmNotes:
Three-beat scene. Beat 1 establishes the city's two campaign-defining rules (credits move everything; lethal weapons stay on the ship). Beat 2 is the investigation work-beat — all five existing disciplineChallenges live here. Beat 3 fires the unsigned threat message on a ~90-minute fictional timer (or earlier if Maya's Marker safety net is pulled). The wall of silence is the scene's POINT, not its obstacle — the threat message is the resolution, not the failure case.

Existing disciplineChallenges block is unchanged and remains canonical. Beat gmNotes reference each challenge by ID (sc-a3s1-*) and indicate which beat it's live in. Top-level read-aloud above is the scene-set; each beat carries its own read-aloud.

VARTH'S ROLE: 'Man in the Chair' from the Banshee — measured, dry, complete sentences, gets quieter when angry. Voice-overs in every beat. He's already done the prep work the heroes don't see (wired the customs bribe, queued the spaceport-slice intel, has a list of contacts to suggest). The team is competent because Varth makes them look competent.

Hand off to adv3-p1-s2 (The Industrial Connection) the moment the table heads for the lift after Beat 3.

=== FORESHADOW PLANT — 137.12 SENSOR HIT (P3 S5 SETUP) ===
The Banshee's docking sweep flags background chatter on slave-circuit band 137.12 from a bulk hauler in low Bespin orbit. This is the FIRST mention of the frequency in the campaign — it lands here so that when the Final Table (P2 S4) hands the crew the 137.12 wafer, the players already recognize the number, AND so that when the *Assiduous* jams that exact band over Bespin in P3 S5, the players understand viscerally why the Operator lane is closing. Do NOT spell out the future use. Just plant the band and let Varth's dry observation log it. Reward any PC who pursues it: a Tech/Wits Resist 3 confirms that 137.12 is one of the legacy slave-circuit boarding bands used by Indemnity-class bulk transports — and that anything broadcast on it can be heard by anyone in orbit, including the Empire.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Arrival on the Cloudscape
encounters.trigger: The crew steps off the Banshee onto a Cloudscape Platform
encounters.description:
Cloud City is a four-century mining colony in restless motion — Ugnaught riggers, Wing Guard in mismatched armor, gambling barkers, Tibanna prospectors, refugees with bedrolls. The crew has Varga's name, the suspicion he is here, and nothing else. The first hour is sensory orientation — the smell of Tibanna venturi exhaust, the sound of hovertruck horns, the stretch of orange cloud below the platform railings.

Maya is the local-knowledge voice. She has run cargo through Bespin before — back when she was working a Tibanna leg out of Nar Shaddaa — and the city's rhythms are familiar to her in a way nobody else on the crew can match. Walking off the platform with the others, she clocks the Wing Guard captain on the take by his stance alone ("That's the posture of a man who already knows who's paying him this week — don't trust the uniform"); she points out the Ugnaught riggers on the next platform over who notice the crew, register them, and deliberately look away ("That's not fear of strangers. That's fear of being seen knowing strangers"); she nods at the venturi exhaust columns rising off the refinery decks below and tells the crew which way the wind blows in the lower terraces if anyone has to run on foot.

Varth is on encrypted comms from the Banshee, in a sensor-analysis support role — he is reading public traffic feeds, port schedules, and Wing Guard transponder pings, and will flag patterns Maya cannot see from the ground. He is not narrating the city; he is watching its data shadow.
encounters.tactics:
NO DICE — orientation only. Players make first impressions, choose lodgings, ask Maya what she's seeing on the ground or Varth what the sensor picture looks like from above. Drop one ambient detail per PC: a Wing Guard officer who lingers a beat too long on the crew, a child running a betting pool on the next ore shipment, a dead Ugnaught being quietly removed by maintenance droids two platforms away. End the beat when a PC asks the first concrete question about how to find Varga.

VOICE NOTE: Maya does the local color (cantinas, dock crews, Ugnaught contacts, Wing Guard rumor — street-level smuggler knowledge from prior runs through Bespin). Varth does sensor analysis and signals intelligence over comms. Do NOT have Maya narrate Imperial fleet movements or sensor sweeps — that is Varth's lane. Do NOT have Varth narrate cantina rumor or street-level color — he has never been to Cloud City. Do NOT name-drop a Baron Administrator — In Year 5 IE (15 BBY), Calrissian is still twelve years out from running Cloud City; today the city is governed by a long-established mix of guilds (Tibanna, Ugnaught labor, casino), Wing Guard, and the corporate concessionaires Figg & Associates have run the refining contract through for nearly four centuries. Cloud City is OLD, not new — built ~400 BBY by Lord Ecclessis Figg with Ugnaught labor (Figg traded their freedom for the construction work). The city deliberately keeps its head down to avoid drawing the full weight of the Imperial garrison; the Payday Illusion is that everything looks like paradise while every smile is bought.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — The Wall of Silence
encounters.trigger: Crew begins asking about Varga in cantinas, dock offices, ore brokers
encounters.description: Every contact closes up. Bartenders pour drinks and look past the question. A Sullustan ore broker rolls down his shutter mid-conversation. A spice runner the crew finds in a back booth pays for her drink and leaves before the question lands. The pattern is too clean to be ordinary fear — Varga has paid the entire underworld to not see the crew coming. The wall is comprehensive. Within ninety minutes, the crew has talked to a dozen people and learned exactly nothing.
encounters.tactics:
RUNNING THE BEAT:
Use the existing Charm / Insight / Investigation discipline checks (per the scene's disciplineChallenges block).
• Failed checks burn time without intel.
• Succeeded checks confirm the wall AND earn one warm contact — an off-duty rigger willing to whisper a single sentence: "Try the Works. The Ugnaughts have a problem too."
• Wins or losses both lead to Beat 3. The wall is the scene's point, not its obstacle.

MAYA'S MARKER — GM SAFETY NET:
Opt-in. Narrative only. NO DICE.

WHEN TO FIRE:
• Table is going in circles, OR
• 30+ real minutes have passed without forward motion toward Beat 3.

MAYA'S OFFER ON PRIVATE COMM:
"I've got a marker I can pull. There's an Ugnaught in The Works named Krygg — I ran a Kessel run for him three years back, the kind of run he should not have asked me to make and I should not have said yes to. He owes me, deep. I haven't pulled this one in three years and I'd rather not, but if you all are stuck up there, I make the call and we get a name and a place out of him by the time you finish your drinks. Your call."

PLAYER CHOICE — ACCEPT OR DECLINE:
• ACCEPT — Maya makes the call off-screen. Within ten in-fiction minutes she comes back on comm: "Krygg. The Works. Maintenance Bay Seven. He says come quiet, come in twos, and come now." The Beat 3 unsigned message STILL fires on its ~90-minute timer — when it lands, the crew gets two converging confirmations pointing at the same place (Krygg's name + Ugnaught-cadence linguistic read), so Beat 3 reads as confirmation rather than revelation.
• DECLINE — Beat 3 fires as written. Maya does not push. The marker stays unpulled and remains available later in the campaign as a one-time GM tool (note it in the campaign log).

IMPORTANT — DO NOT MISREAD THIS TOOL:
This safety net does NOT replace or short-circuit the existing Charm / Insight / Investigation paths to the Ugnaught lead — those remain active throughout. It is an opt-in narrative escape hatch for a stalled table, not a parallel solution path. No dice. No Resist. The cost is fictional only — Maya burns a personal favor she would rather have kept.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — The Unsigned Threat
encounters.trigger: After ~ninety minutes of stonewalling
encounters.description:
Every crew datapad chimes at the same instant — an unsigned text message routed through three relays Varth cannot trace. STAY OUT OF THE INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT. NO WARNINGS AFTER THIS ONE. The message has no signature but it is in Basic, written in the precise idiom of someone whose first language is not Basic.

Maya reads it once, twice, and then once more out loud — and the third reading is the one where it lands. "That's an Ugnaught. I've crewed with a few — they learn Basic from Imperial training holos and the cadence sticks weird, real formal, all the contractions sanded off. This wasn't written by the Hutt's people. This was written by somebody scared, who's trying very hard to sound like he's not." She glances at the routing line. "Three relays in, terminating somewhere in the Industrial District. The Parliament of Guilds. Not Varga."

Varth, on comms, dry: "Confirmed. I had the same read about thirty seconds behind you." A beat. "Good catch."

The crew has their first real lead.
encounters.tactics:
NO DICE — delivery beat. The message is the scene's pivot. Maya's Basic-idiom read is free intel (she has actually crewed with Ugnaught riggers; Varth has not). PCs may also try a Slicing or Insight check on the routing to add detail (Resist 1) — success surfaces that the relays terminated in a maintenance bay in The Works. Either way, the crew leaves Beat 3 knowing The Works is the next target.

VOICE NOTE: The linguistic-cadence call belongs to Maya here — she has the lived crew experience to make it. Varth's one-line dry follow-up is the entire shape of his contribution to this beat; do not expand it, and do not have him beat her to the read. If the GM fired the Beat 2 'Maya's Marker' safety net and the crew accepted it, Krygg's name from that earlier ping plus this Ugnaught-cadence read converge cleanly — both arrows point at The Works. If the safety net was declined or unfired, this beat carries the lead by itself, exactly as before.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — The Service Lift
encounters.trigger: Crew commits to The Works
encounters.description: The crew finds the only public service lift down to the industrial decks — operated by an off-duty Wing Guardsman named Hessel who asks no questions and charges five credits per head. The descent is forty stories. The lift is open-sided. The temperature climbs. The light gets dimmer and oranger. Hessel says one sentence on the way down, without looking at anyone: "Ugnaughts are scared. Whatever you came down here for — be quick about it. Wing Guard rotation through this lift in twenty minutes." He does not elaborate. The lift opens onto the catwalk-maze of The Works.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — atmospheric transition. Hessel's sentence is a free contact-of-convenience the GM may use later (he can be called for an unscheduled lift back up if the crew is on the run, but only once, and he expects ten credits per head for the favor). The twenty-minute timer is a soft pressure for Beat 5 / scene s2 — establish it but do not enforce it; it is meant to make the Ugnaught conversation feel urgent, not to create a hard fail state.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Hand-off to The Works
encounters.trigger: Crew steps off the lift into The Works catwalk
encounters.description: The Works is steam, sodium-orange light, the constant gargle of Tibanna venturis, and the bustle of a thousand Ugnaught riggers and engineers between shifts. Two Ugnaughts are visibly waiting for the crew at the third catwalk junction — Fyren, short and ink-stained, and Krygg, taller and arms-crossed. They are not threatening. They are nervous. Fyren raises a hand, palm out, and gestures the crew toward Maintenance Bay 7. The threat-message senders have come to meet the threat-message recipients. Adventure 3 Scene 2 picks up there.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — handoff beat. The Ugnaught greeting is unmistakable; if the crew chooses to ignore it and explore The Works on their own, Fyren and Krygg follow patiently and make the same gesture again at the next junction. They will not give up. The scene ends when the crew enters Maintenance Bay 7 (s2 trigger).

disciplineChallenges.context: Tracing the threatening message to its source.

control.failure: Message was routed through multiple proxies. Dead end on the digital trail. Whoever sent it knows their opsec.
control.mastery: Origin traced AND you recover fragments of the sender's other transmissions — they've been monitoring Varga's operations for months. This is an ongoing operation, not a one-off.

effect.fleeting: The encryption is commercial-grade, not military. Narrows it to Cloud City locals with access to public infrastructure.
effect.masterful: Digital forensics trace the origin to the Ugnaught Parliament of Guilds — an industrial administrator terminal. Someone with legitimate access.
effect.legendary: Full trace: the specific terminal, the time of transmission, and residual login credentials that point to a maintenance foreman named Fyren.

disciplineChallenges.context: Getting locals to talk about Varga. Everyone is bribed or scared.

control.failure: Stone wall. Nobody talks. Varga's money is louder than your charm.
control.mastery: The bartender not only directs you but slips you a hand-drawn map of the industrial levels where the Ugnaughts work. Marked with safe routes that avoid Varga's patrols.

effect.fleeting: A nervous glance toward the industrial district. Somebody almost talked before thinking better of it. You know the general direction.
effect.masterful: A bartender whispers: 'Try the Ugnaughts in the Works. They hate him more than they fear him.' First solid lead.
effect.legendary: The bartender gives you the Ugnaughts' names — Fyren and Krygg — their work shift, and the specific maintenance bay where they take breaks. Clean approach guaranteed.

disciplineChallenges.context: Moving through Cloud City without attracting Varga's informants.

control.failure: A street rat clocks you and runs toward the cantina district. Varga may know you're here within the hour.
control.mastery: Clean movement AND you identify two of Varga's informant positions. Can be avoided for the rest of the stay.

effect.fleeting: You stick to secondary corridors. Slower, but no obvious tails. Can't be sure you're clean though.
effect.masterful: Clean movement. No one flags your presence. Standard counter-surveillance protocols hold.
effect.legendary: Ghost-level movement. You map Varga's entire informant network on the tourist level as you move through it. Know exactly where the blind spots are for future operations.

disciplineChallenges.context: Creating a cover story for why you're on Cloud City.

control.failure: Cover is thin. First serious scrutiny will blow it. Don't get stopped by Wing Guard.
control.mastery: Cover is so good that Wing Guard actively assists you — offers directions and local guidance, treating you as welcome visitors.

effect.fleeting: Basic tourist cover. Won't survive a records check but it handles casual encounters.
effect.masterful: Convincing cover as prospectors or traders. Wing Guard wouldn't look twice.
effect.legendary: Airtight cover with planted digital records. If anyone checks, they find a legitimate business history, docking permits, and a Tibanna purchasing license.

disciplineChallenges.context: Reading the threatening message — is it a real threat or a warning?

control.failure: Reads as a genuine threat. Approach with caution — may be a trap.
control.mastery: Not just scared — the sender is watching the recipients right now. They're testing whether you're Varga's agents or potential allies.

effect.fleeting: The tone is off for a real threat. More nervous than menacing. Probably not an ambush.
effect.masterful: The tone is scared, not hostile. Whoever sent this is trying to protect themselves, not threaten you. A cry for help disguised as a warning.
effect.legendary: Specific linguistic patterns: industrial jargon, formal grammar, and a Ugnaught idiom translated into Basic. The sender is an educated Ugnaught trying to make contact safely.

beats.title: Approach & Customs
beats.readAloud:
Civilian docking bay 327 is small, well-lit, and entirely full of strangers in uniform. Three Cloud City customs officers wait at the boarding clamps the moment the ramp lowers — courteous, well-dressed, and absolutely unwilling to release the Banshee until the ship is searched. Their leader, a tired human woman with a lieutenant's bar on her collar, recites the words she has clearly recited four hundred times since the start of the month: "By order of Cloud City Spaceport Authority and the Cloud City Wing Guard, we are obligated to inspect inbound vessels for contraband, undeclared weapons, and unregistered passengers. Please cooperate. The process takes approximately ninety minutes."

Behind her, mounted on the bay wall in Basic, Bocce, and Ugnaught script: NO LETHAL WEAPONS BEYOND THIS POINT. KNIVES AND STUN BATONS PERMITTED. VIOLATION: CONFISCATION + EXPULSION FROM CLOUD CITY.

Varth's voice resolves on the private comm — already three steps ahead, already amused:

"Varga ran from Takodana the night you breached the fortress at Blackwind Point. The Glorious Chariot — his yacht, the one you watched lift off Maz's lake — pinged Cloud City spaceport sixteen days ago. Nothing's docked under that registry since. He's here. He's deep. I've already wired the lieutenant's office fifteen hundred credits to waive the inspection — she'll find it in her department's discretionary account before she finishes pretending to scan the manifest. The weapons restriction, however, is real and is enforced. Leave the heavy gear on the ship or hide it well. Wing Guard catches you with a long-arm in the main concourse and you're on a freighter to Anoat by sundown."
beats.gmNotes:
Set the city's two campaign-defining rules cleanly:
  1. CREDITS MOVE EVERYTHING — Varth pre-pays the customs bribe so the table doesn't have to roll for a non-decision. Establish this as the modern adv3 voice (the team is competent because their handler is competent).
  2. LETHAL WEAPONS STAY ON THE BANSHEE — knives and stun batons are fine in main thoroughfares; anything bigger has to be hidden or left behind. This rule binds adv3-p2-s4 (Final Table) — every player needs to know it NOW so the casino-floor weapons restriction reads as setup, not arbitrary GM fiat.

NO DICE in this beat. If a PC volunteers to negotiate the bribe themselves rather than letting Varth handle it, run sc-a3s1-charm (Presence/interact, R3/P3) live and treat the Fleeting tier as "you saved Varth a thousand credits." Otherwise narrate Varth's wire transfer; the customs lieutenant pockets a discreet datachit and waves the Banshee through with apologies for the inconvenience.

If players try to smuggle weapons past customs anyway, that's their choice — narrate the customs scan as routine and let them attempt to hide the weapons (Stealth or Deception at GM's discretion, R3/P3). Discovery means confiscation of that weapon and a noted violation against the offending PC's name in the Wing Guard system; multiple violations during the adventure trigger expulsion at the worst possible moment in adv3-p2.

Hand off to Beat 2 the moment the customs party leaves the bay and the crew steps out into Cloud City proper.

beats.title: A Wall of Silence
beats.readAloud:
Outside the docking bay, Cloud City unfolds. Wide promenades polished to a mirror shine, fog-glassed lifts threading between platforms, Wing Guards in white-and-blue stationed every fifty meters with stun batons clipped to their belts and carbines slung at parade-rest. The crowds are thick: prospectors arguing exchange rates with currency-exchange droids, finely dressed offworlders trailing protocol droids of their own, Ugnaughts moving in tight defensive packs that everyone else pointedly ignores. Every cantina is full. Every hotel marquee reads NO VACANCY. Every street has someone selling commemorative Sabacc Tournament chips that will be worthless in a week.

You start asking about Varga. The answers don't vary. Bartenders pour drinks without comment and find reasons to be elsewhere when the conversation shifts. A Devaronian fixer who would normally name his price for the right question waves you off mid-sentence and pays his own tab on the way out the door. A spaceport tech who almost says something thinks better of it and walks away. By the third hour, the pattern is unmistakable. This is not "I don't know." This is won't say.

Varth on comm, dry as paper:

"That's bribed silence. A different problem from honest ignorance, and a more solvable one. Two angles. One: Cloud City's spaceport logs run through a Wing Guard security post on Platform Twelve — slice in from there and you can pull the Glorious Chariot's docking record, if it still exists. Two: work the corners. Somebody on this rock hates Varga more than they fear him. Find them."
beats.gmNotes:
THIS IS THE SCENE'S MAIN WORK-BEAT. All five existing disciplineChallenges are live here.

LIVE CHALLENGES (existing block, unchanged — just slotted into this beat):
• sc-a3s1-investigation (Wits/assess, R3, P3) — slicing the Wing Guard terminal at Platform Twelve. Fleeting tier surfaces the Glorious Chariot's logged port of origin (Takodana) and confirms it docked sixteen days ago with all subsequent docking-bay records erased. Masterful narrows to a Parliament of Guilds terminal as the source of the data tampering. Legendary names Fyren as the Ugnaught who ran the erasure script.
• sc-a3s1-charm (Presence/interact, R3, P3) — bartenders, fixers, off-duty riggers. Masterful gets Fyren and Krygg by name; Legendary adds shift schedule and Maintenance Bay Seven as the meeting location.
• sc-a3s1-stealth (Reflex/interact, R3, P4) — moving through informant-laced corridors clean. Masterful clocks two Varga informants and lets the crew avoid them; Legendary maps the entire informant network on the tourist level.
• sc-a3s1-deception (Presence/interact, R2, P3) — building a tourist or prospector cover the Wing Guard accepts. Useful as protection while running the other checks.

WINS OR LOSSES BOTH LEAD TO BEAT 3. The wall is the scene's POINT. Failed checks burn fictional time without intel; succeeded checks earn the warm contact (off-duty rigger willing to whisper "Try the Works. The Ugnaughts have a problem too.") and accelerate Beat 3's read-aloud (the trace will be cleaner because they're already pointed in the right direction).

GM SAFETY NET — "Maya's Marker" (OPT-IN, NARRATIVE ONLY, NO DICE): If the table is going in circles, OR 30+ real minutes have passed without forward motion toward Beat 3, the GM may fire this safety net. Maya pings on private comm: "I've got a marker I can pull. There's an Ugnaught in The Works named Krygg — I ran a Kessel run for him three years back, the kind of run he should not have asked me to make and I should not have said yes to. He owes me, deep. I haven't pulled this one in three years and I'd rather not, but if you all are stuck up there, I make the call and we get a name and a place out of him by the time you finish your drinks. Your call."

PLAYER CHOICE — accept or decline:
• ACCEPT: Maya makes the call off-screen. Within ten in-fiction minutes, she comes back on comm with: "Krygg. The Works. Maintenance Bay Seven. He says come quiet, come in twos, and come now." The crew now has a confirmed lead. The Beat 3 unsigned message STILL fires on its ~90-minute timer — when it lands, the crew gets two converging confirmations pointing at the same place (Krygg's name + the Ugnaught-cadence linguistic read), which lets Beat 3 read as confirmation rather than revelation.
• DECLINE: Beat 3 fires as written. Maya does not push. The marker stays unpulled (and remains available later in the campaign as a one-time GM tool — note this in the campaign log).

This safety net does NOT replace or short-circuit the existing Charm/Insight/Investigation paths to the Ugnaught lead — those remain active throughout. It is an opt-in narrative escape hatch for a stalled table, not a parallel solution path. No dice. No Resist. The cost is fictional only (Maya burns a personal favor she would rather have kept).

beats.title: The Threat
beats.readAloud:
Datapads chirp in unison — every member of the crew, the same instant. The message has no header, no sender, no signature. Six lines of plain text:

"Stop digging. The drop is long, and the gas pressure is high. Go home."

That's all. No demands, no follow-up, no signature.

The Banshee's astromech traces the routing the moment Maya forwards her copy: three commercial proxies, two of them legitimate Cloud City forwarders, the third a public terminal in an industrial sub-level. SECTOR U357 — PARLIAMENT OF GUILDS — ADMINISTRATIVE.

Maya pulls up the city map on the comm channel and drops a marker: two transit-lift transfers and a long walk down through warehousing, refining, and waste-recovery to get to the door.

Varth, warmer now — almost relieved:

"That's not a threat. That's somebody terrified you'll lead Varga to them. People who want you dead don't write. Go down there and say hello. Quietly. And take the long way — every Wing Guard between you and Sector U357 will remember a heavily armed party heading for The Works."
beats.gmNotes:
This beat fires on the natural ~90-minute fictional timer regardless of what the table accomplished in Beat 2 (or earlier if Maya's Marker was pulled — see Beat 2 gmNotes).

The message text is verbatim and non-negotiable. The trace is automatic — the astromech runs it, no roll required, the result is always the same Sector U357 destination. This is the scene's exit ramp, not a puzzle.

LIVE CHALLENGE (optional):
• sc-a3s1-insight (Presence/assess, R2, P2, OPTIONAL) for any PC who wants to read the message itself. Fleeting tier: "scared, not hostile." Masterful tier: "cry for help disguised as a warning." Legendary tier: identifies the sender as an educated Ugnaught using formal Basic grammar with one translated Ugnaught idiom — "the gas pressure is high" is an Ugnaught labor expression for "people are watching."

Hand off to adv3-p1-s2 (The Industrial Connection) the moment the table heads for the lift.

scenes.title: The Industrial Connection
scenes.readAloud:
The descent into The Works takes three transit lifts and forty minutes. The cars get smaller at each transfer, the lighting dimmer, the air heavier with the smell of hot metal and something faintly chemical underneath. Humans thin out and Ugnaughts thicken — by the bottom transfer you're the only non-Ugnaughts in the car. The other passengers don't make eye contact. A foreman with a half-burned ear glances at your party once, grunts something that doesn't translate, and looks away.

Sector U357 is a long catwalk above a refining floor, the catwalk lined with scuffed durasteel doors marked in Ugnaught script and Basic. A small placard at the end identifies the office you want: PARLIAMENT OF GUILDS — SECTOR U357 ADMINISTRATIVE.

The door slides open at your touch. Inside: a dozen Ugnaught clerks at terminals, looking up in unison. Long silence.

Then one of them — smaller than the others, visibly shaking — grabs the sleeve of the Ugnaught beside him and squeals in panic:

"I told you they would find us! I told you! You've brought them down on us — they'll kill us all because you couldn't leave it alone — "

The second Ugnaught wrestles his coat free, exasperated rather than frightened.

"Krygg, ENOUGH. We don't know they work for the Hutt. They might be here to help."

He turns to the crew. Tired eyes, ink-stained hands, the body language of a labor administrator who has been awake for thirty hours.

"My name is Fyren. The one trying to climb inside his own jacket is Krygg. Come into my office. We have very little time, and you have already made a great deal of noise getting here."
scenes.gmNotes:
The Krygg/Fyren character moment is the scene's hook — play it as written. Krygg = pure terror, Fyren = exhausted operator. They are not enemies; they sent the Beat 3 threat in s1 hoping to scare the heroes off precisely because they're afraid the heroes will lead Varga's enforcers right to them.

THE STAKES (Fyren delivers in his office, conversational not read-aloud — keep the table engaged with questions rather than monologue): When Varga set up shop in Cloud City eight months ago, he started bribing Ugnaught riggers inside Figg & Associates to siphon spin-sealed Tibanna gas off the official manifest. Figg noticed. They couldn't identify which Ugnaughts were on the take, so they pressured the Parliament to crack down on ALL Ugnaughts. Over eight months, Ugnaught reputation on Cloud City has collapsed — wage cuts, restricted work zones, the loss of three Guild seats on the city council. Fyren and Krygg are watching their community get strangled for crimes a handful of bribed riggers committed. They want it stopped. This is WHY they're risking the contact, not just what.

THE TRADE (Fyren's offer): The Parliament has tracked Varga's most recent siphon operation to Refinery Platform 13. There is a shipment going out within the hour. If the heroes stop it — Fyren is careful to say they don't insist the corrupt riggers be killed, but neither will they mourn the loss — the Parliament will hand over everything they know about how Varga's payment from the Empire is being routed through the Cloud City Sabacc Tournament.

LIVE DISCIPLINE CHALLENGES (existing block, unchanged):
• sc-a3s2-persuasion — convincing Fyren the heroes can be trusted with the operational intel up front (he holds back the tournament details until the deed is done unless he's sold hard).
• sc-a3s2-insight — reading whether Fyren is hiding more than the reputation collapse (he is not — what you see is what you get; the Empire connection is real, the Ugnaughts know it, they want help).
• sc-a3s2-investigation — pulling Parliament records to corroborate the reputation-collapse story; useful as a relationship-builder, not a gate.
• sc-a3s2-charm — winning over the room of clerks rather than just Fyren and Krygg; Legendary tier earns a quiet word from a Sullustan clerk that the corrupt rigger boss at Refinery 13 is named Greel Trask, has a wife and two children, and "would fold if cornered." This intel feeds the s3 parley path directly.

Hand off to adv3-p1-s3 (The Refinery Rumble) once the deal is struck. Krygg will follow the heroes to the lift, wringing his hands, and mumble blessings in Ugnaught at their backs as the doors close.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Inside Maintenance Bay 7
encounters.trigger: Crew enters Maintenance Bay 7 with Fyren and Krygg
encounters.description: The bay door cycles shut. Fyren snaps a portable signal jammer on. Krygg drags two crates over and gestures the crew to sit. The hand-written threat note is on the workbench, weighted with a hydrospanner. Fyren confirms, without prompting, that he wrote it. Krygg confirms, with prompting, that he co-signed reluctantly. They open the floor: the crew came down armed for hostiles and instead they have two terrified Ugnaught Guild administrators who have been waiting six months to find a crew like theirs.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — entry beat. Establishes the room and the two NPCs. Players may want to scan for surveillance (free Insight: the jammer is real, the bay is clean) or to refuse the seats and stay standing (Krygg shrugs and stays standing himself). Beat ends when a PC asks the first real question — that triggers Beat 2.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Sitting Down with Fyren and Krygg (Conversation Overlay)
encounters.trigger: A PC asks the first real question of the Ugnaughts
encounters.description: Fyren and Krygg invite the crew's questions in earnest. This is the structured social scene — the Fyren-Krygg conversation overlay. Launch the [fyren-krygg-the-works] conversation from the Conversation panel. The two Ugnaughts share a single comfort meter; Fyren is the diplomat voice, Krygg is the pragmatist voice. The conversation can deliver tournament handover intel, the cashier (Mandelbrot) characterization, the Imperial undercover (Arandis) tell, the Nuvo wound, and — at high comfort — a Wing Guard service-corridor keycard.
encounters.tactics: GM ACTION: Open the Conversation panel and launch [fyren-krygg-the-works]. Comfort starts at 3. Story topics about the Tibanna siphon and Nuvo HOLD comfort. Business topics about the handover are neutral. Probe topics about Guild complicity cost 1 comfort each. Krygg's tell is his knuckle-cracking — when comfort drops, he cracks. When it rises, he sits. The hard exit is Krygg pulling Fyren out by the collar at Comfort 1. The conversation ends when accessible topics run out, when comfort drops to 1, or when the GM is ready to hand off to Beat 3.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — The Trade Offered
encounters.trigger: After the conversation overlay closes — assuming the Ugnaughts did not bolt
encounters.description: Fyren lays it out plainly: stop Varga's thugs from stealing a Tibanna shipment at Refinery Platform 13 tonight, and the Ugnaughts will deliver everything they promised — the tournament handover diagram, the cashier brief, the service-corridor keycard if comfort earned it. Krygg adds the constraint: no Ugnaughts on the operation, no Ugnaught names in any reporting back to Wing Guard or station authorities. The crew is the cudgel. The Ugnaughts are the eyes.
encounters.tactics:
NO DICE — deal beat. The richness of the trade is gated on the conversation outcome:
  • Comfort 4-5 at end of Beat 2: full intel package + Wing Guard keycard + safe-house promise (used in p3-s1 Gauntlet).
  • Comfort 3: full intel, no keycard, conditional safe-house (Krygg has to think about it).
  • Comfort 2: handover diagram only — no cashier, no air-tram option, no keycard.
  • Comfort 1 (Krygg pulled Fyren): Refinery 13 objective only. No further intel. The trade is the scene's deliverable.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — The Quiet Way Out
encounters.trigger: Trade is struck, intel exchanged
encounters.description: Krygg walks the crew to the south service lift — the one Wing Guard does not rotate through, operated by an Ugnaught named Tev who owes Krygg a debt. The lift takes the crew up to Platform 87, three stories below their lodgings, a quiet exit. Krygg gives one parting line, gruff: "Bring our gas back. Then come find us. Cantina on level 312, the night after. We will know your faces." Fyren does not speak as the crew leaves. He watches the bay door cycle shut behind them.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — exit beat. The south lift route is a free re-entry the crew may use to return to The Works any time during the adventure without burning Hessel's favor. The cantina rendezvous on level 312 (the night after Refinery 13) is a real beat the GM should honor — it lands in a later interlude and is where Krygg cooks the bad meal he promised in the conversation if comfort hit 4+.

disciplineChallenges.context: Convincing the Ugnaughts you're allies, not Varga's agents.

control.mastery: Full trust earned immediately. They introduce you to the wider Ugnaught resistance network — six more workers who've been documenting Varga's operation.

effect.fleeting: Grudging willingness to talk. They'll share what they know but won't commit to anything further. Transactional.
effect.masterful: Fyren and Krygg open up. They describe the gas siphoning operation — scale, timing, and the Trandoshan enforcers who guard the refinery.

control.failure: Hard to read. Ugnaught body language is unfamiliar. Could be genuine or a setup.
control.mastery: Genuine — AND you notice Krygg keeps glancing at a datapad. He's been recording Varga's shipments. Physical evidence exists.

effect.masterful: Genuine terror and anger. They've been exploited. This is real — and it's been going on for months.
effect.legendary: These two have been planning their own resistance for a year. You're not recruiting them — they've been waiting for someone exactly like you.

disciplineChallenges.context: Reviewing the Ugnaughts' evidence of Varga's gas siphoning.

control.failure: Evidence is circumstantial. Need more proof before acting.
control.mastery: The manifests show a destination code that matches Project Leviathan logistics. Direct connection between Varga's Tibanna and the Imperial superweapon project.

effect.fleeting: Numbers don't add up — more Tibanna is leaving Cloud City than the legitimate contracts account for. Something is being siphoned.
effect.masterful: Shipping manifests confirm military-grade Tibanna going to Imperial warships. The scale is staggering — this is industrial-level theft.
effect.legendary: Complete paper trail: production numbers, skimmed quantities, routing through shell companies, delivery coordinates, and Imperial authorization codes. Prosecution-quality evidence.

disciplineChallenges.context: Building rapport with the Ugnaughts for a deeper alliance.

control.failure: They'll trade info for the refinery job but nothing more. Purely transactional.
control.mastery: Deep alliance formed. The Ugnaughts offer their maintenance access tunnels as a permanent safe network throughout Cloud City. Game-changing mobility advantage.

effect.fleeting: Friendly but cautious. They'll help with the refinery but need to see results before committing further.
effect.masterful: They commit fully. Will provide ongoing support — safe houses, equipment, information. A real alliance.
effect.legendary: Blood oath (Ugnaught tradition). They pledge their guild's resources: safe houses, fabrication equipment, encrypted comm network, and a dedicated guide for the industrial levels.

scenes.title: The Refinery Rumble
scenes.readAloud: Refinery Platform 13 hangs three kilometers below the main city, suspended by atmospheric repulsors in the gas giant's roiling cloud band. The transit pod ride down takes nine minutes through alternating bands of amber and bruised purple cloud, the platform's running lights barely visible until you're a hundred meters out. The wind is a continuous low howl across exposed catwalks — not violent, but constant, the kind of sound that makes conversation a chore inside the first hour.
scenes.gmNotes:
Three-beat scene. Beat 1 is recon (intel-gathering checks live). Beat 2 forks into STRIKE or PARLEY based on the table's choice — both branches converge at Beat 3. Beat 3 is the Indemnity reveal — the most important narrative beat in p1, plants the seed Maya will detonate in adv3-p2-s2.

PARLEY PATH: Restored from the DoD original. The corrupt rigger boss Greel Trask (named in s2 if the table earned the Sullustan clerk's tip) is genuinely terrified — he took the bribe eight months ago for his family and has been living with the cost. He'll surrender in exchange for safe passage off Cloud City. The Trandoshan mercenaries he hired don't care about Ugnaught politics — once Trask folds and stops paying, they'll lift off rather than die for an Ugnaught who won't honor the contract.

STRIKE PATH: Runs the existing combat encounter exactly as designed — see encounters block. Trandoshan mercenaries plus corrupt Ugnaught riggers, catwalk terrain, environmental hazards (rupture splash zones, steam pipes).

VARTH'S ROLE: Coordinates from the Banshee. Updates the team on the loading progress every two minutes during Beat 1 (creates time pressure). Goes silent during combat (Beat 2 STRIKE). Re-engages at Beat 3 for the Indemnity read — and his careful word-choice when Maya asks the slave-ship question is THE moment that flags him to attentive players.

MAYA'S ROLE: Quiet through Beats 1-2. Speaks at Beat 3, reading the manifest. HER LINE IS VERBATIM AND NON-NEGOTIABLE — the campaign hinges on the players hearing her ask the question.

pacing.risingAction: The ambush. Fighting on catwalks in wind and steam.

control.failure: Spotted at the platform edge. Trandoshans scramble to defensive positions. No surprise round.
control.mastery: Perfect approach AND you identify the sentry rotation gap — 90 seconds when the entire east platform is unmonitored. Sabotage window.

control.mastery: You vault the machinery so fast you end up behind the Trandoshan line. They're flanked.

effect.masterful: Confident movement. Use the machinery and catwalks to close distance and gain positional advantage.

disciplineChallenges.context: Disabling the shuttle to prevent the Trandoshans from escaping with the gas.

control.failure: Partial shutdown. Production slows but doesn't stop. Varga will notice within hours, not days.
control.mastery: Clean shutdown AND you plant a data siphon on the control systems. Future operations will provide real-time production data.

effect.fleeting: Emergency shutdown triggered. The refinery stops but the restart sequence is automated — it'll be back online within a day.
effect.masterful: Clean shutdown with safety lockouts engaged. Requires a qualified engineer to restart — Varga loses days of production.

disciplineChallenges.context: Searching the Trandoshan leader's datapad after the fight.

control.failure: You still get the headline reveal: the gas is bound for the Imperial Navy, and the bulk-runs ship is the Indemnity — flagged as a slave transport with living cargo in slave-circuit holds. What you do NOT get is the deeper schedule data, headcounts, or the buyer chain — datapad encryption locks all of that. Slave-transport intel is unambiguous on any outcome.
control.mastery: Full data AND you discover a shipping code that matches Project Leviathan logistics manifests from Adv1. The Tibanna fuels the superweapon.

effect.fleeting: Standard recovery: the gas is destined for the Imperial Navy, and the ship taking the bulk runs is the Indemnity — flagged in the manifest as a slave transport. Living cargo, in slave-circuit holds.
effect.masterful: Full The Indemnity manifest: bulk-run schedule, average headcount per transport (three hundred plus), and the Tibanna load percentages per voyage. The slave-transport detail is unambiguous.
effect.legendary: Complete Imperial shipping network: routes, schedules, quantities, the Indemnity as the primary bulk carrier, and three sister ships running parallel. Enough intel to track or intercept future slave shipments.

beats.title: Approach
beats.readAloud:
The platform is a flattened octagon roughly the size of a freighter pad. Four storage tanks the size of housing blocks ring the perimeter. A short-haul YT-class shuttle is parked center-platform, its cargo ramp down and its crew ramp up. Worker-class spotlights light the loading area in hard white. From your approach angle on the catwalk, you can see figures moving in and out of the spotlight — not many, maybe eight or nine total — loading slim metal canisters onto the shuttle.

The wind covers most sound. A man could shout from twenty meters and you wouldn't hear it.

Far above, just barely visible through a break in the cloud band, a much larger silhouette is holding station — a windowless bulk hauler the length of three city blocks, running lights doing the slow regular blink of an unmanned automated vessel. It's been parked up there for hours. Maya's voice on comm, half to herself: "Imperial automated tanker. Pre-programmed milk run. The Empire flies a fleet of those through every Tibanna colony — load, dump, load, dump, no crew, no log."

Varth's voice, low:

"That shuttle's a YT-class haul. Holds maybe thirty canisters, tops. They're loading number twelve as you watch. You've got time, but not much. Decide your approach now — once those canisters are aboard and the ramp closes, the shipment lifts off and we lose this."
beats.gmNotes:
RECON BEAT. Two existing checks live here:

• sc-a3s3-stealth (Reflex/interact) — getting closer without being clocked. Masterful tier reveals the rigger boss (an Ugnaught named Greel Trask, named in s2 if the Sullustan clerk's tip was earned) standing apart from the Trandoshans, on a comm. Legendary tier overhears his half of the conversation: he's complaining that the Trandoshans want double-rate combat pay, and he doesn't have authorization for it from his Hutt contact.
• sc-a3s3-investigation (Wits/assess) — reading the manifest stencils on the canisters being loaded. Masterful confirms military-grade gas pressure ratings (consistent with weapons-system feed lines, not civilian heating). Legendary identifies the destination tag — bound for an Imperial bulk freighter currently in low Bespin orbit.

Both checks inform the Beat 2 choice. The Stealth Masterful/Legendary results in particular let the table know that Trask is buyable. The Investigation Legendary primes the players for the Beat 3 reveal so it doesn't come out of nowhere.

TELEGRAPH THE AUTOMATED HAULER (read-aloud addition). The unmanned bulk tanker visible above the cloud band is the same class of vessel that the Empire will ram into the Indemnity during adv3-p3-s5 (Skirmish Over Bespin) as cleanup. Maya's offhand line about 'pre-programmed milk runs, no crew, no log' is the seed. If a PC pursues it with a Tech or Investigation check (Resist 3), they confirm: these haulers run a closed nav-routine that can be redirected remotely from any Imperial nav-relay; the Empire could turn one into a kinetic weapon at will. Do NOT spell out the future use. Just plant the fact. When the gas-hauler comes screaming down on the Indemnity in P3, the players will recognize the silhouette and the moral weight of the moment will land as 'we saw this ship before, and we knew what it could do' instead of as a contrived deus-ex.

After the recon checks, hand the table the explicit choice: STRIKE or PARLEY. Do not let it ambiguously slide into combat. Make them pick.

beats.title: Strike
beats.readAloud: You move on the loading area. The first Trandoshan to spot you raises a slug carbine and roars something in Dosh that doesn't need translation. Greel Trask drops into a service hatch and slams it behind him. The other Ugnaught riggers scatter for cover behind canisters. Three Trandoshans fan out across the catwalks, and the one nearest the shuttle ramp flips a switch on the cargo lift — locking the shuttle in place. They mean to hold the platform.
beats.gmNotes:
STRIKE BRANCH. Runs the existing combat encounter exactly as designed in the encounters block. Trandoshan mercenaries plus 2-3 corrupt Ugnaught riggers, catwalk terrain, environmental hazards live (gas-tank rupture splash zones, steam-pipe scald damage).

LIVE CHALLENGES:
• sc-a3s3-ranged — combat checks during the firefight.
• sc-a3s3-athletics — catwalk traversal, dodging splash zones, leaping the cargo gap to the shuttle.
• sc-a3s3-tech — disabling the cargo lift to trap the shuttle on the platform; or hot-wiring it to launch the shuttle EMPTY into the cloud band as a denial action if combat goes badly.

Greel Trask is in a service hatch under the platform — if pursued AFTER the Trandoshans are dealt with, he surrenders immediately, on his knees, citing his wife and children. Treat his datapad as the source of the Beat 3 manifest reveal in this branch.

Converges at Beat 3 the moment the platform is secured.

beats.title: Parley
beats.readAloud:
You step into the spotlight with hands visible and the Ugnaught rigger boss's name on your tongue. The Trandoshan nearest the ramp brings his carbine up reflexively but doesn't fire. Greel Trask freezes. He's mid-thirties for an Ugnaught, scar across the bridge of his snout, wearing a foreman's harness over street clothes that don't match.

His eyes flick from your party to the Trandoshans to the cargo shuttle and back. He says, in Basic with a thick Ugnaught accent:

"Whatever the Parliament is paying you, I will double it. In credits. Right now. Off the books. I have a wife. Two children. I never wanted any of this. Please."
beats.gmNotes:
PARLEY BRANCH. Trask is genuinely terrified. The bribe eight months ago was a one-time decision he has been paying for ever since — Varga's enforcers visit his apartment monthly to "remind" him of his obligations, his wife stopped sleeping six weeks ago, his elder daughter has started asking questions he can't answer.

Trask will surrender the entire shipment AND the operational details (every bribed rigger's name, every drop schedule for the next thirty days, the comm-handle of his Imperial contact) in exchange for safe passage off Cloud City for himself and his family. The Parliament can grant this — Fyren has the authority and will honor the deal if the heroes confirm Trask's family will be relocated cleanly.

THE TRANDOSHANS ARE MERCENARIES. Once Trask folds and stops paying them, they'll fade back to their shuttle and lift off rather than die for an Ugnaught who won't honor the contract. NO DICE on the Trandoshan walk-off — it's narrative if the parley with Trask succeeds.

LIVE CHALLENGE (Trask's surrender):
• sc-a3s2-persuasion (re-used from s2) OR sc-a3s1-charm (re-used from s1) at R3/P3 — the GM picks based on which discipline the PC's pitch leans on. The lever is Trask's wife-and-children fear, not credits or threats.
• Failure on the parley check → Trask panics, triggers the alarm, and the STRIKE branch begins as written, with Trask's panic granting the Trandoshans one free round of action before the heroes can act.

If parley succeeds, Trask hands his datapad to the heroes voluntarily. The Beat 3 manifest reveal happens immediately — no body to search.

Converges at Beat 3.

beats.title: The Datapad
beats.readAloud:
The platform is yours — combat-quiet or trade-quiet, depending on how the last twenty minutes went. The shuttle sits on its ramp, half-loaded. Twelve canisters stenciled with military pressure ratings are aboard; twenty-three more are still chained in the bay. Whatever the Empire was supposed to receive in this run, it's not getting it.

On the platform foreman's body — or in Greel Trask's surrendered datapad, depending on your route — you find the manifest. The destination tag isn't a unit. It isn't a quartermaster. It isn't an Imperial fuel depot. It's a single ship name, repeated on every canister:

THE INDEMNITY — BULK CARRIER — IMPERIAL NAVY — LOW BESPIN ORBIT.

Maya's voice on comm. Quiet:

"That's a slave ship. The Indemnity-class are converted bulk haulers — they don't need armed guards because the cargo is in chains. Why is the Empire sending weapons-grade Tibanna gas to a slave transport?"

A long pause. Then Varth, careful, choosing his words:

"That's a question for later. We have what we came for. Get back to the lift. The Ugnaughts owe us a tournament briefing."
beats.gmNotes:
THE THE INDEMNITY REVEAL is the most important narrative beat in p1. It plants the seed Maya will detonate in adv3-p2-s2 and act on alone in adv3-p3 (per campaign-bible.md "Maya's silence about the slave ship" / "Maya's fate is optional").

LIVE CHALLENGE (one final use of s3's investigation):
• sc-a3s3-investigation lives here ONE LAST TIME for any PC who wants to dig deeper. Fleeting tier confirms the destination tag and the orbital position. Masterful tier pulls the Indemnity's last seven port calls (every one a slave-trade hub — Kessel, Klatooine, the Gozanti exchange at Sriluur). Legendary tier finds a passenger manifest fragment — three hundred and eighty-four numbered "units," no names, all logged as boarded at Klatooine four standard days ago. Children counted separately (sixty-one).

DELIVER MAYA'S LINE VERBATIM. The campaign hinges on the players hearing her ask the question. Her tone is not horrified — it's clinical. The horror is what she is NOT saying.

TELEGRAPH MAYA'S OBSESSION — START HERE. The orbital moral choice in adv3-p3-s5 (Skirmish Over Bespin) only lands as 'we should have seen this coming' if the GM plants Maya's tells starting RIGHT NOW. After her line, hold the silence on comm a beat longer than is comfortable. If the crew is back aboard the Banshee at the end of the scene, the Pilot or anyone watching her sees her open the manifest on a side console and read the children-counted-separately number twice. She does not speak to anyone for the next ten minutes. If a PC asks her about it directly, she answers flatly: "I knew a Indemnity-class once. From the inside." She will not elaborate. Note the moment in the campaign log — this is the first of THREE telegraphs (P1 S3, P2 S2, P3 S3 dock-side beat) that earn the moral choice.

DELIVER VARTH'S DEFLECTION VERBATIM. He knows what the Indemnity is. He is choosing to wait. Players who notice — particularly anyone running an Insight check unprompted — should be told privately: "Varth's voice was different on that line. Not warmer. Not colder. Just careful, the way a man speaks when he's choosing each word." Note Varth's deflection in the campaign log. This is foreshadowing for adv3-p3 and beyond.

Hand off to adv3-p1-s4 (The Imperial Mark) when the lift starts climbing back to Cloud City proper.

scenes.title: The Imperial Mark
scenes.readAloud:
The lift back from The Works takes the same forty minutes the descent took, in reverse. Nobody speaks much. The Indemnity manifest sits on three of the crew's datapads, the destination tag glowing in the reader-light: a slave ship in low Bespin orbit, expecting weapons-grade Tibanna gas it will not receive.

By the time you reach Sector U357 again, Fyren is already waiting for you in his office. He has been waiting, you suspect, since the moment the lift began to climb.
scenes.gmNotes:
Four-beat scene — the role-assignment scene that the Tournament Tracker UI's ttroster panel binds to. This is the WORST-OFFENDER scene from the original prose — gmNotes used to just say "WALK THE TABLE THROUGH THE FOUR ENTRY PATHS." Now structured as:

  Beat 1 — The Ugnaughts Pay In Full (Fyren delivers the briefing; the entire courier-laundering mechanism is explained)
  Beat 2 — The Lobby (the Yerith Bespin tableau; tiered Investigation/Insight reveals Arandis and his entourage)
  Beat 3 — Marking the Bagman (Varth's tactical brief on what Arandis will actually do at the table)
  Beat 4 — Choosing Your Angle (the four entry paths, with each one tied to a specific action against Arandis)

The existing five disciplineChallenges (sc-a3s4-investigation, -deception, -stealth, -tech, -insight) are slotted into beats 2 and 3.

PRESERVE THE INTENT of the original gmNotes ("Multiple PCs may take different paths within the same tournament — the menu is designed to support a party split. Read the four options to the table together so the choice is informed.") — restated in Beat 4 with concrete linkages between each path and what it lets you DO about Arandis.

The Tournament Tracker UI ttroster panel binds to Beat 4. Each PC's role declaration persists into the panel's roster blob and surfaces at adv3-p2-s1.

decisionPoints.prompt: Key Decision: Entry Path to the Tournament

options.label: Competitor — pay the buy-in and play
options.consequence: 10,000 credits per seat from Varth's stake. Direct access to Arandis's table at the Final Table. Wears the comm-jamming pin (no comlink contact with the crew while seated).

options.label: Security — hire on with Mandelbrot's house team
options.consequence: 500 credits/day plus a Mandelbrot-issued weapons permit each PC can use to bring legal ordnance into the casino floor. Free movement, no table access.

options.label: Spectator — bluff in as a plus-one or Cloud City official
options.consequence: Charm or persuasion check at the velvet rope (Resist 3, failure = remembered face that comes back at the Heist scene). Free intel-relay role; cannot influence cards.

options.label: Dirty Money — take Switch's contract on Koroma Moro
options.consequence: Switch comms the Banshee Day 1 with the offer. Crew agrees in principle now, commits Day 3. Helping Moro win the Final Table = no Imperial card-arrangement transfer = no slave-circuit frequency = no The Indemnity lead.

encounters.name: Path A — Competitor
encounters.trigger: PC wants a seat at the table
encounters.description: Varth covers a 10,000-credit buy-in per registered seat from the Banshee's operating fund. The competitor is the only role with eyes on Arandis's actual play, but they are also the only role wearing the casino's comm-jamming pin once seated — comlinks dead, intel must be passed in person during break beats.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — stake commitment. Mark 10,000 credits per registered competitor off the crew sheet. The competitor PC inherits the cover-identity work from s5 prep and the comm-jamming pin (see environment mechanic in adv3-p2-s1).

encounters.name: Path B — Casino Security
encounters.trigger: PC pitches Mandelbrot's floor manager for a guard slot
encounters.description: The Royal Casino's house security is hiring tournament-week temporaries. The pay is 500 credits per day per PC, paid in marked Bespin chips, AND each hire is issued a Mandelbrot weapons permit — a small ID disc that lets the bearer carry one Restricted-tier weapon onto the casino floor without confiscation. The crew can use the permits to walk concealed ordnance past the door scanners. Security PCs have free run of the floor, the back rooms, and the count-room corridor.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE for the hire itself — Mandelbrot's manager is short-staffed and grateful. The weapons-permit detail matters: each permit-bearing PC can bring one Restricted weapon (anything legalStatus <= 2/r) onto the floor. Security PCs are also the natural intel-relay for competitor PCs once the comm-jamming pin goes live.

encounters.name: Path C — Spectator (Bluff Entry)
encounters.trigger: PC tries to enter the casino without a buy-in or a guard badge
encounters.description: The casino velvet rope admits plus-ones of registered competitors and accredited Cloud City Tourism Bureau officials. A spectator PC pitches one of those covers to the Twi'lek concierge (Vass) at the door. Charm or persuasion against Resist 3 — if the cover is plausible (rehearsed in s5 or backed by a fake Bureau credential), the bluff lands; if it is thin, Vass remembers the face and that recognition surfaces at the Heist scene as a +1 Resist on any Deception or Stealth check that passes through the lobby.
encounters.tactics: ROLL — Charm or Persuasion vs Resist 3. Failure consequence is real (remembered face -> +1 Resist at adv3-p2-s5 lobby pass-through). Spectator PCs are the natural crowd-side intel-relay once the comm-jamming pin goes live; they can pass meatspace notes to competitor PCs during break beats.

encounters.name: Path D — Dirty Money (Switch's Contract)
encounters.trigger: Day 1 of the tournament — Switch comms the Banshee privately
encounters.description: Switch — the Twi'lek information broker the crew met in adv2 — opens a private comm to the Banshee on Day 1 of the tournament and forwards it to whichever crewmember answers. He pitches plainly: he has a man at the table named Koroma Moro. He wants Moro to win. Switch will pay the crew five to seven percent of Moro's take (negotiable, top of the range if Moro wins clean) for any help they can provide — feeding Moro reads, distracting his table opponents, or actively cheating on his behalf. Switch needs an answer in principle Day 1 so he knows whether to keep Moro at the table; the crew's actual commit point is Day 3, after the Maya/Varth The Indemnity argument in adv3-p2-s3 has surfaced what is really on the ship Fioro's code unlocks.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE for the pitch itself. The crew can agree in principle Day 1, defer (Switch waits until Day 2 then drops it), or refuse. Actual commit lands Day 3 — see adv3-p2-s3 (Pressure Cooker). CRITICAL: helping Moro win at the Final Table BLOCKS the slave-circuit frequency reveal. No card transfer = no 137.12 = no Indemnity lead. The fork genuinely competes with the Imperial intel-grab.
