beats.title: The Ugnaughts Pay In Full
beats.readAloud:
Fyren receives you in the same cramped office as before. He looks slightly older than he did six hours ago. Krygg pours water from a chipped enamel pitcher. No one sits.

Fyren keeps his end of the bargain. Eight months of Parliament intelligence, spread across his desk in printed sheets because he doesn't trust the Cloud City data network for this conversation:

The Empire is paying Varga for something. They have been paying for nine months. The payments do not run through Imperial ledgers — they run through a single courier who carries the credits, in transferable hard-currency wafers, to a public-facing commercial venue and loses them at gambling. A predesignated winner at the same table collects. The losses are written off as recreational expenditure on the courier's officer ledger. The Empire's books stay clean. Varga's proxy walks away with hard credits.

The next handover, Fyren tells you, is the Cloud City Sabacc Tournament. Three days from now.

"Start with the Yerith Bespin Hotel. The Royal Casino is sealed for tournament prep — half the Wing Guard is standing watch on the doors, you won't get within fifty meters until the tournament opens. The Yerith is where the courier and his entourage stay. Watch the lobby. You will know him when you see him."
beats.gmNotes:
Pure exposition beat. NO DICE. Fyren delivers the briefing because he owes the heroes a debt — let him talk uninterrupted unless players actively interrupt with questions, in which case answer them in his voice.

THE COURIER LAUNDERING MECHANISM is the entire thesis of part 2 — make sure every PC understands it before moving on. If the table seems unclear, have Krygg ask a clarifying question and let Fyren patiently answer:
  Q: "Why don't they just transfer the credits directly?"
  A: "Because Imperial credit transfers leave records, and this transaction does not exist."
  Q: "How does the proxy know to win?"
  A: "The courier and the proxy do not need to know each other. The courier loses on schedule. Whoever is at his table when the schedule executes is the winner. Varga's proxy is at every table the courier sits at. The math works itself out."

Fyren does NOT know the courier's name yet — that's Beat 2's discovery. He knows only that the courier will be at the Yerith Bespin and that the tournament is the venue.

The Royal Casino is closed; the Yerith Bespin is the lead. Hand off to Beat 2 the moment the table leaves Sector U357. Krygg, again, will follow them to the lift wringing his hands.

beats.title: The Lobby
beats.readAloud:
The Yerith Bespin's lobby is the kind of space that announces its budget without trying. Carrara-pattern carpet woven through with platinum thread; floating crystal chandeliers held aloft by repulsor pads so quiet you have to look up to confirm they're working; a check-in counter of polished red wood manned by six staff in matched livery. The clientele is dressed for it — Core nobles, corporate princes, the very rich pretending to be incognito.

A scene is already underway at the counter. A human male in his fifties, dressed in mid-Core noble fashion, is berating a clerk at sustained volume — something about his suite, the wine in his suite, and the temperature of the wine in his suite. The clerk is enduring it with the expression of someone whose job depends on her ability to endure it. Heads are turning. Several aren't.

Across the lobby, eight people stand in a quiet cluster waiting for the noble to finish. Four of them are men — middle-aged, dressed in identical dark suits, similar enough in build and bearing that you find yourself looking from one face to another. Two are humanoid women — pale-skinned, with patterned hair in shades that don't occur in nature, posture relaxed but eyes never still. The remaining two are a Sullustan and a Twi'lek, both carrying datacases.

Varth, almost gentle:

"That's your courier. The shouting man. Name on the hotel registry is Lieutenant Armen Arandis — Imperial Naval Intelligence, payroll attached to Sector Group Bespin. Take a long look at his entourage before you decide your approach. The shouting is theater. Everything in that lobby right now is theater."
beats.gmNotes:
THE ESTABLISHING TABLEAU the original scene was missing. Run a tiered Investigation check (sc-a3s4-investigation, Wits/assess, R3, P3 — treat the noble + entourage as the target):

• Fleeting tier: The two humanoid (Theelin) women across the lobby aren't entourage. They're scanning the room methodically. Bodyguards.
• Masterful tier: The four "retainers" in matched suits are similar enough in face and frame to be siblings. Closer attention reveals they're identical past the differences a hard life writes — old scars, broken noses set at slightly different angles. Same genetic stock.
• Legendary tier: The four are clones — old-pattern, the same template the Republic's Grand Army drew from. They moved to private security after Order 66; this kind of work pays them better than the Empire's pension would. Treat as a Galactic Lore freebie if the Investigation result lands at Legendary.

If no one rolls Investigation, fall back to Insight (sc-a3s4-insight, Presence/assess, R2, P2) reading the shouting itself:
• Fleeting: The noble is angry but the staff he's berating isn't actually trying to defuse him, like they've been told to absorb it.
• Masterful: The entire scene is a delay tactic, designed to occupy lobby attention while the entourage observes who else is in the room.
• Legendary: Arandis is checking faces against a list, and you saw his eyes pass over you exactly once before sliding away.

After Beat 2, the table knows: the courier is Arandis, his "bodyguards" are professional Theelin operators, his "retainers" are clones. Hand off to Beat 3.

beats.title: Marking the Bagman
beats.readAloud:
The argument at the counter resolves — abruptly, as scripted theater does. Arandis nods curtly, the clerk produces a fresh keycard, and the noble strides away from the counter with his entourage falling in around him in a loose protective formation. They take the lift to the upper floors. The lobby returns to its quiet murmur within ninety seconds, as though nothing happened.

You retreat to the lobby bar — a curved length of black stone tended by a Bothan in a cream tunic — and order drinks while Varth's voice resolves what you just watched:

"Arandis is a mathematician. Specifically, an officer of the Imperial Naval Intelligence accounting branch. He memorizes pip values to seven decimal places. At a sabacc table, he can lose a precise amount of money over a precise number of hands without ever appearing to throw the game — every loss looks like statistical noise. That is the entire skill set the Empire is paying him for. He is here to lose two hundred and fifty thousand credits to a designated winner over the course of the tournament. Your job is to either be the designated winner, or be in a position to know who is — the moment the wafer changes hands."
beats.gmNotes:
This beat sets the player objective in concrete terms. The mechanism (Arandis loses on a schedule, proxy collects, wafer changes hands) is now fully on the table. NO DICE for the briefing itself.

OPTIONAL CHALLENGES live for any PC who wants to push further:

• sc-a3s4-stealth (Reflex/interact) — following Arandis's entourage from the lobby to the upper floor and clocking his suite number. Fleeting tier identifies the floor (twenty-second). Masterful tier identifies the suite (2207, the Bespin Sky Suite — the hotel's largest). Legendary tier confirms the entourage's room assignments (clones in 2206 and 2208 flanking, Theelin bodyguards inside the suite proper, Arandis in the master bedroom; Sullustan and Twi'lek aides in 2205 across the corridor). This intel feeds the SECURITY entry path in Beat 4 and any infiltration of the suite during adv3-p2.

• sc-a3s4-tech (Wits/interact) — slicing the Yerith Bespin guest network from the lobby. The hotel's WAP is unsecured for guests but the staff network requires authentication. Fleeting confirms Arandis's group has booked through Friday. Masterful pulls his itinerary (every meal, every spa appointment, every casino slot — including a private viewing of the Royal Casino's tournament floor on Thursday afternoon). Legendary recovers a draft message from Arandis's hotel terminal to an unspecified Imperial recipient: "Asset arrived. Window is firm. Loss schedule attached."

• sc-a3s4-deception (Presence/interact) — chatting up the Yerith Bespin staff under cover (concierge, bell staff, valet) for soft intel. Useful for the Spectator entry path (cover legitimacy at the Royal Casino's public gallery).

Hand off to Beat 4 once the table is satisfied with their intelligence picture. There is no hard gate — but if every PC has skipped the optional checks, prompt: "Anyone want to take a closer look at Arandis or his suite before we talk about getting you into the tournament?"

beats.title: Choosing Your Angle
beats.readAloud:
Maya's voice cuts across the comm, brisk:

"Okay. We've got him. Tournament starts in seventy-two hours. The Royal Casino opens its registration window at noon tomorrow. We need to decide how each of you gets through that door — because once you're inside, every entrance has its own footprint, its own permissions, and its own way to put hands on Arandis's wafer when it moves."

She pulls up a four-quadrant brief on every crew datapad:

  COMPETITOR  ·  SECURITY  ·  SPECTATOR  ·  DIRTY MONEY

Varth, weighing in from the ship:

"Pick the angle that fits you. There is no wrong answer. We can field two of you in one role and one each in two others — the casino floor is large enough to hide six familiar faces if they aren't standing together. Talk it through. You have until noon tomorrow to commit."
beats.gmNotes:
THIS IS THE ROLE-ASSIGNMENT BEAT — the Tournament Tracker UI ttroster panel binds here. Walk the table through the four entry paths and what each one DOES against Arandis specifically. Multiple PCs may take different paths within the same tournament; the menu is designed to support a party split. Read the four options to the table together so the choice is informed.

COMPETITOR (10,000 credit buy-in, auto-charged via the tracker):
A seat at the tournament. By Day 2 the field will narrow to the point where Arandis's table is identifiable. Direct line of sight on the wafer when it moves at the Final Table. Best for any PC with sabacc skill, gambling cover, or the credits to burn. Buy-back-in available at 2,000 credits if eliminated mid-Day 1.

SECURITY (free, requires Mandelbrot pitch):
Hired into Jacc Mandelbrot's house security team. Access to the casino's back-of-house, security feeds, and — critically — a justifiable reason to sweep Arandis's hotel suite during play (Mandelbrot's contract gives him search authority over registered competitors' rooms during the tournament for cheating-prevention purposes). Best for any PC with Stealth, Tech, or a credible intimidation profile. Surfaces the cheater-catch beat in adv3-p2-s1 (Creeska the Rodian).

SPECTATOR (free, requires invitation cover):
The casino's gallery seats overlook every felt. Permitted to circulate, photograph the action for the Holonet sports feed, and sit close enough to read facial tells. Best for any PC with Insight, social-engineering skill, or a press-credential cover. Spectators are the only role allowed to carry recording gear onto the floor — useful when the wafer transfer happens in plain sight.

DIRTY MONEY (free, but conditional):
Switch (the Bothan fixer the crew met previously, now operating a Cloud City satellite office) approaches one PC with a side contract: 5,000 credits up front to ensure that a specific Twi'lek competitor named Koroma Moro wins the tournament. Switch will not say who wants Moro to win, only that the contract is firm and the payout doubles if Moro wins clean. This is ALSO an entry path — Switch can buy any PC into a "private investor" role attached to Moro's table, with floor access in a different doorway than the other three entrances. Picking Dirty Money does NOT preclude the other entry paths for OTHER PCs — but it sets up the moral pivot that fires in adv3-p2-s3. The PC who takes Dirty Money is committing the crew to the possibility that Moro, not Arandis's proxy, wins the wafer.

PERSIST EACH PC'S ROLE in the Tournament Tracker UI ttroster panel before ending the scene. The roster blob feeds adv3-p2-s1 directly — every entry-path mechanic surfaces in the Day 1 scene based on what was selected here.

Hand off to adv3-p1-s5 (The Buy-In) once every PC's role is locked.

scenes.title: The Buy-In
scenes.subtitle: Tournament Eve
scenes.readAloud:
The Cloud City sun goes red over the cloud-band by 1900 local. By 2000 the crew is on the casino's mezzanine — not yet on the floor, but inside the ring, in the brick-walled administrative warren that runs behind the Royal Casino's public face. The smell up here is fresh paint and ozone from new comm gear. Tomorrow morning this corridor will be sealed.

You spend the first two hours finalizing the work of the entry-path scene: paying buy-ins where buy-ins are owed, badging in with Mandelbrot's security manager where guard slots were taken, locking down spectator covers, and — if Switch's offer was accepted in principle — opening a quiet line to a Twi'lek named Koroma Moro who will be at the table tomorrow.

At 2200 a Sullustan with sun-creased skin and a tournament organizer's pin — Jacc Mandelbrot's house manager, another Jacc by coincidence, who answers to "Jacc the Other" to keep things from getting confusing — pulls the crew into a brick-walled office off the count room. He goes around the table once before he speaks, taking each crewmember's measure and asking the same simple question:

"And you are entering as — ?"

He waits for each answer. He nods at each one. He notes none of them down — he's already been briefed, this is verification — and when the circle is closed he leans back against his desk and runs through the casino's standing rules in the flat tone of a man who has given the same briefing four hundred times.

Comm-jamming pins issued to every competitor — pinned to the lapel, active for the duration of every hand. Buy-back-in available at two thousand credits when a player gets sick mid-round, paid in advance, processed at the cage in under sixty seconds. Five named players to watch — three of them long-standing tournament veterans, one a first-year wildcard, one (he says with a particular flatness) a player whose previous tournament appearances have ended in disputes. Three exits from the casino floor. All three close on lockdown. Lockdown happens at the discretion of the house and is not, he wants to be clear, a hypothetical.

Tomorrow the doors open at standard daybreak. He shakes each crewmember's hand, wishes them a good night, and asks — politely but with weight — that they not embarrass him.

The walk back to the Banshee through the casino's emptying back corridors takes twenty minutes. Maya has the galley lit when you board. There's stew. There's caf. No one talks much.
scenes.gmNotes:
TOURNAMENT-EVE BEAT. The Assiduous arrival has been moved out of this scene and into the new adv3-p2-s2 (Message from the Banshee), where it lands during the tournament itself with the Switch commit. This scene is now a clean preparation beat — final cover-checks, buy-in ledger, Mandelbrot security briefing, and one quiet round at a cantina or the Banshee galley if the table wants it.

NO DICE on the Mandelbrot briefing — the rules he names are mechanics that bind the next scene (comm-jamming pin, buy-back-in, named players to watch). Surface them here so the table knows them before they sit down.

THE COVER-STORY ROLL-CALL: When Jacc the Other walks the table asking each PC "And you are entering as — ?", give every PC the floor for one beat to declare their cover in their own voice. This is not a roll — it is a player-facing moment to lock in the entry path emotionally as well as mechanically. The Tournament Tracker roster panel should reflect each declaration exactly. If a PC declared Dirty Money, Jacc's nod will be a fraction slower than the others (he knows; he doesn't say so).

THE FIVE NAMED PLAYERS: Mandelbrot's "five to watch" list maps to the five named NPCs at the tournament (Lieutenant Armen Arandis, Lady Fioro, Silas Draver, Creeska the Rodian, Koroma Moro). The "previous appearances ending in disputes" line is Mandelbrot flagging Creeska as a known cheat without naming him directly — adv3-p2-s1's catch-the-cheater beat depends on this seed. Players who pay attention will register the implicit warning.

LIVE CHALLENGE (optional):
• sc-a3p1s5-charm — any PC wanting to read Jacc the Other for additional intel beyond the public briefing. Fleeting tier earns the floor map. Masterful tier confirms the lockdown procedure (six Wing Guards plus Mandelbrot's eight house security on the doors, all three exit corridors flooded with non-lethal gas at command). Legendary tier gets a personal aside — Jacc admits he has been told by Mandelbrot to keep particular eyes on Lady Fioro's table, though he will not say why.

Hand off to adv3-p2-s1 (Day 1) at standard daybreak.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Mandelbrot's Standing-Rules Briefing
encounters.trigger: Crew assembles in the count-room office for the house briefing
encounters.description: Jacc Mandelbrot — Sullustan, sun-creased, the casino's house manager and head of the count room — runs through the standing rules in the flat tone of a man who has done this hundreds of times. (1) Every competitor wears a comm-jamming pin once seated. The pin produces a vocoder static field that kills any outgoing comlink signal from within five meters of the wearer. Removal of the pin while inside the casino is grounds for immediate expulsion and forfeit of buy-in. The pin can be spotted on a competitor by anyone watching for it (skulduggery or investigation, Resist 3) but spotting it does not let you defeat it; it only confirms what is in play. (2) Buy-back-in is permitted: when a competitor gets sick mid-round (it happens; the casino looks the other way as long as the paperwork is clean), an eliminated player can re-enter for a flat 2,000-credit fee paid to the cashier. Use it as the rescue valve. (3) Five named players are entered: Lt. Armen Arandis (Imperial cover, plays cold), Lady Mirana Fioro (Hapan, plays for keeps), Silas Draver (loud, drunk-acting, sober — Mandelbrot has already flagged him to floor security), Creeska (Rodian, two prior expulsions for card-marking on other circuits — watch him), and a Twi'lek named Koroma Moro who arrived alone and paid in marked Bespin chips. (4) Three exits from the casino floor — the velvet entrance, the service corridor that runs to the count room, and the upper-deck fire stair to the air-tram platform. Lockdown closes all three on the manager's call.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — rules briefing. These are mechanics that bind tomorrow's scenes. End beat with Mandelbrot shaking each PC's hand and asking, politely, that they not embarrass him.

encounters.tactics: NO DICE — atmosphere. Honor whichever direction the players take it. End scene at standard daybreak; hand off to adv3-p2-s1 (Day 1 — Catch the Cheater).

scenes.title: The Elimination Rounds — Day 1
scenes.subtitle: Day 1 — Catch the Cheater
scenes.readAloud:
The Royal Casino is a loud, smoky, aggressive establishment where prospectors gamble away fortunes and refugees bet their last credits. Over fifty competitors crowd the tables. The air is thick with Corellian whiskey, Ryll spice smoke, and the mechanical whir of shuffling droids.

Every seated competitor is wearing a small black pin on their lapel — Mandelbrot named it last night. The pin produces a vocoder static field; comlink chatter dies within five meters of any wearer. Whatever you need to pass to a teammate at the table today, you pass face-to-face during the breaks.

You notice four players worth watching: a flamboyant human named Silas Draver who seems drunk but isn't, a cold Hapan noblewoman named Lady Fioro who bankrupts a weeping Dug in the first hour, a Twi'lek named Koroma Moro who keeps to himself, and a Rodian named Creeska who is, even to a casual eye, doing something with his sleeve that he should not be doing.
scenes.gmNotes:
DAY 1 of the tournament. The headline beat is Catch the Cheater (security PC) / Make a Read (competitor PC) — Creeska, the Rodian, is palming a card-marker. The forcing function is Mandelbrot's tournament-administrator gavel at end of session: tables reset, half the field is eliminated by the cashier's posted bracket, downtime block follows, Day 2 opens fresh.

The comm-jamming pin is now LIVE for every competitor PC. Intel must be passed in person during break beats. Security PCs, spectator PCs, and the Banshee crew are the relays.

The Switch Dirty Money offer (if the crew accepted in principle in adv3-p1-s4) is in play but does not commit until Day 3 (adv3-p2-s3 Pressure Cooker). Switch may send a Day 1 reminder ping if the GM wants to keep the temptation visible — flagged in Beat 4 below.

=== HOW TO RUN SABACC — RESOLUTION MODEL (READ FIRST) ===

This campaign uses ABSTRACTED SABACC, not card play at the table. Sabacc is a SKILL CHALLENGE driven by the Competitor PC's relevant disciplines (Charm/bluff, Wits/calculation, Insight/read), NOT a real card mini-game. This is a deliberate choice: the tournament arc spans four sessions of real-world play, and asking the table to learn a card system on top of the campaign rules will collapse the pacing.

MECHANICS: Each tournament day resolves as ONE headline check (Resist 3 baseline, +1 each day) representing the day's play. The headline check IS the existing per-day Competitor scene-challenge (sc-a3s2-bluff/charm/insight Day 1, the equivalent in p2-s2/s3/s4 for Days 2/3/4) — do NOT stack a separate sabacc check on top of those. The non-Competitor side beats and parallel-tracks scenes use their own challenges and resolve independently. Outcome bands:
• Critical Failure: bust out — the PC is eliminated from the tournament, switches to a non-Competitor role for remaining days (Spectator / Security observer / Dirty Money runner)
• Failure: short stack — the PC survives the day but starts the next day at a disadvantage (-1 to next sabacc check)
• Success: chip leader at table, hand of choice (the PC may pick one bonus per day — see below)
• Masterful: clean win — bonus + advantage on the next day's check
• Legendary: dominant — bonus + advantage + an unprompted observation about another player's tell (auto-progresses one Read on Fioro/Arandis/Draver/Moro)

DAILY BONUS MENU (Success+ pick one): (a) overhear a side-table conversation — bridge to a parallel-track beat; (b) credit-spot a tell on one of the named players; (c) request a specific seat reassignment for Day 2-3-4; (d) bank chips toward a Day 4 buy-back if eliminated on Day 3.

WHAT IF A PC BUILT FOR SABACC? Reward the build. A PC with a sabacc-tagged background, ability, or trait gets +1 to all tournament-day checks AND may re-roll one failed check per day. They are still using the abstract resolution — they just get more bites. This protects the build investment without making the gambler PC the only person who matters.

WHAT IF THE GROUP WANTS REAL CARDS? Sabacc rules-lite is fine for the FINAL TABLE (adv3-p2-s4) ONLY — the climactic single hand where the 137.12 transmission happens. Days 1-3 stay abstracted. Even at the Final Table, the canonical card-arrangement reveal is non-negotiable: Arandis's losing hand is what it is, regardless of what the PCs draw. Frame the cards as flavor over a fixed narrative outcome.

GM PROMISE TO THE TABLE AT THE BUY-IN (adv3-p1-s5): Tell the players explicitly, in session: "Sabacc resolves with checks, not cards. The Competitor's spotlight is one check per day plus the parallel-tracks scenes. Everyone else has a daily thread." This sets expectations and lets sabacc-built PCs know their build still matters.

=== PARALLEL TRACKS — 4-DAY CADENCE FOR NON-COMPETITOR PCs ===

READ THIS BEFORE RUNNING DAY 1. The single biggest failure mode of the tournament arc is letting the felt dominate while non-Competitor PCs sit on their hands. Sabacc is one PC's spotlight; the other three need their own scenes EVERY day, hard-cut between threads like a heist movie. Every tournament day breaks into four blocks the GM should pre-cast roles for:

• MORNING SESSION (felt) — Competitor PC at the table, runs ~30 min real-time
• MIDDAY BREAK (relay window) — face-to-face intel pass, comm-jamming pin off only here
• AFTERNOON SESSION (felt) — Competitor PC at the table, ~30 min real-time
• EVENING DOWNTIME (parallel beats) — every non-Competitor role gets a scene

ROLE-BY-ROLE DAILY SCAFFOLD (cycle whichever the player picked at adv3-p1-s5 The Buy-In):

SECURITY PC (working Mandelbrot's house security):
• Day 1: Catch the Cheater (Creeska) — flagged headline beat
• Day 2: Vet the spectator gallery — clock an Imperial paymaster contact, surface Arandis sightings
• Day 3: Sweep Lt. Arandis's hotel suite during his absence (Skulduggery; finds payday courier itinerary fragment)
• Day 4: Position for the Final Table — establish sightlines, plant ear, pre-position for Draver's Heist (P2 S5)

SPECTATOR PC (working the gallery and cantina):
• Day 1: Mark the four players-of-interest from Maya's read; notice Fioro's bodyguard rotation pattern (45-min intervals)
• Day 2: Shadow Arandis between sessions — he visits the same booth twice, talks to a Rodian fixer
• Day 3: Tail Fioro from the casino to her suite; identify her permanent escort (the bodyguard who later names Docking Bay 4414)
• Day 4: Crowd-control eyes during Final Table — first to spot Draver's crew moving in

DIRTY MONEY PC (working Switch's fork, if active):
• Day 1: Receive Switch's reminder ping; meet Moro's runner in the cantina to confirm payment terms
• Day 2: Begin the disinformation prep — false bracket leaks, distract Imperial bookkeeping
• Day 3: COMMIT POINT in P2 S3 Pressure Cooker — the fork locks in or dies here
• Day 4: Execute the Moro favor (whatever the table negotiated) during the Draver's Heist chaos

MAYA / BANSHEE CREW (off-felt support — and the Indemnity seed):
• Day 1: Flying overwatch + dock-crew gossip; Maya passes Day 1 read on the four players to whoever's in the gallery
• Day 2: Maya reacts to the Assiduous news (see P2 S2) — visible Indemnity tell
• Day 3: Maya goes quieter than usual; the dock contacts she's been working get one more name
• Day 4: Maya's silent solo run begins off-screen during the Final Table chaos (the players will not know)

MANDELBROT (always in play):
• Day 1-4: Tournament-administrator presence, gavel forcing function each evening, willing to brief any role between sessions

GM RHYTHM RULE: never spend more than ~20 minutes of real-time on the felt without cutting to a parallel track. If only one PC is at the table and the others are watching their own characters do nothing, the arc will sag. Cut early, cut often.

FALLBACK: if a role is unstaffed (no PC took that entry path at the Buy-In), Mandelbrot, Maya, or Switch's Toydarian runner covers the gap — but the GM should still stage the scene so that role's information surfaces, just from an NPC mouth.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Reading the Floor
encounters.trigger: Crew enters the Royal Casino floor on Day 1
encounters.description: The first hour of the tournament is observation. Competitor PCs are seated at separate tables (per registration). Security PCs walk the floor on Mandelbrot's rota. Spectator PCs work the rail. The brief is to identify the players who matter: Arandis, Fioro, Draver, Creeska, Moro. Krygg's "plays like a man who has been told what to do with cards" tell from the Ugnaught conversation grants free identification of Arandis to any PC who heard it.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE for free identifications. Each PC may attempt one Sense (sense_spark) check per other named player to read deeper than the surface — Resist 3, failure = surface read only (no deeper detail). End beat after the first hour of observation.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Catch the Cheater (security PC) / Make a Read (competitor PC)
encounters.trigger: Creeska palms his marker during a third-round hand
encounters.description: Creeska is cheating in plain sight. The marker is a thumb-sized chemical applicator that tags high-value cards as they pass through his hands. The tell is a single repeating motion — sleeve, thumb, deck, sleeve — that takes one observation pass to spot if you know what you are looking for. Security PCs can spot it on a skulduggery or investigation check (Resist 3) and hand the evidence to Mandelbrot for a clean expulsion (Mandelbrot Rapport +1). Competitor PCs at Creeska's table can spot it from across the felt on the same check (skulduggery or investigation, Resist 3) and use it to fold strategically against him without triggering a reaction. The CRITICAL trap: if a PC accuses Creeska publicly without first surfacing the marker as evidence, Creeska's pre-paid Bothan witness corroborates that the accusing PC has been hovering and acting suspiciously, and Mandelbrot expels the accuser instead.
encounters.tactics: ROLL — skulduggery or investigation vs Resist 3. SUCCESS: marker spotted, evidence in hand, Creeska expelled, Mandelbrot Rapport +1. FAILURE: PC reads Creeska as merely twitchy, no evidence, no movement. CRITICAL FAILURE PATH: PC who accuses Creeska without spotting the marker first is expelled by the Bothan witness plant. Buy-back-in costs 2,000 credits to re-enter Day 2.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Day One Card Play
encounters.trigger: First competitive session of the tournament
encounters.description: Sabacc is played. Each competitor PC plays through six hands at their assigned table while wearing the comm-jamming pin. The cards themselves matter less than the social tells — bluffs that match cover identity, betting patterns consistent with the brag-and-price the Ugnaughts coached, and the absence of crew-level coordination (no eye contact across tables, no shared bathroom breaks). The pin actively prevents crew comlink relay, so competitor PCs operate solo at the felt unless a security or spectator PC physically walks up and passes a note during a posted break.
encounters.tactics: RUN: Charm or Deception vs Resist 3 per competitor PC for cover-hold under live pressure. Failure = cover slips, +1 Resist on the next Charm/Deception check at the table that day. Each PC who survives Day 1 advances to Day 2; each PC who busts is eliminated and must spend the 2,000-credit buy-back-in fee to re-enter on Day 2 (otherwise drops to spectator role for the rest of the tournament).

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Day One Recess at the Back Bar (and Switch's Reminder)

Spotting the pin on another competitor (to confirm what is in play, not to defeat it) requires a skulduggery or investigation check vs Resist 3 — failure on this spotting check means the PC tries to comlink during the table and gets caught by the floor manager (Mandelbrot Rapport -1, public warning). Removing or disabling the pin while inside the casino is grounds for immediate expulsion and forfeit of buy-in. The pin comes off naturally at the back bar (Beat 4) and at all posted breaks.

scenes.title: The Elimination Rounds — Day 2
scenes.subtitle: Day 2 — Message from the Banshee
scenes.readAloud:
Daybreak. The casino doors open on a thinned field — half the names from yesterday are gone, and the surviving competitors look it. Coffee. Black. Comm-jamming pins on. Tables reset.

You are an hour into the second session when Varth's voice cuts in over the crew's open channel — the spectator and security PCs hear it first; the competitor PCs at the felt do not, because the pin is doing its job.

"We have a problem. A massive energy spike just hit the system edge. An Imperial Star Destroyer just dropped out of hyperspace. It is the Assiduous — Inquisitor Draco's flagship."

A beat of silence on the comm.

"That ship is the clean-up crew. If Arandis loses the money wrong, or if Varga double-crosses them, Draco won't bother with arrests. He'll glass the city to bury the evidence. Pass that to whoever you have at a table. Quietly."

Maya is not done. The same open channel, voice flat, the Indemnity tell still hanging in the air:

"Varth. The *Assiduous* will jam 137.12 the second she gets in range. You know it. Their EW package eats slave-circuit bands for breakfast. If we wait for the orbital play, the override won't punch."

Varth, careful, choosing each word:

"You are correct that the *Assiduous* will jam the band. There is one path the *Assiduous* cannot reach. Bridge override panel. Hard-line. Inside the firmware. But it is on the *Indemnity*. You would have to be physically aboard."

A long pause on Maya's end. Then, quietly: "Understood."

She closes the channel. Anyone watching her on the *Banshee*'s aft camera sees her stand up, shoulder a tool roll, and walk off-camera in the direction of the docking ramp. Varth does not flag it.
scenes.gmNotes:
DAY 2 of the tournament. The headline beat is Message from the Banshee — the Assiduous arrival lands here, mid-tournament, instead of pre-tournament. The relay problem is the whole point: the news comes in over comlink, and the competitor PCs cannot hear it because the comm-jamming pin is on. The spectator/security PCs (or Maya/Varth on the Banshee) must walk it to the table during a posted break.

The Day 2 commit-prompt for the Switch Dirty Money fork is here too — Switch sends his second comm with the same offer and a request for an answer in principle, knowing the crew's actual lock-in is Day 3.

TELEGRAPH MAYA'S OBSESSION — TELL #2 OF 3. Right after Varth finishes his Assiduous warning, Maya's voice cuts in over the SAME open channel — not the spectator's private side-band, the open one — and says, "And the Indemnity. If Draco glasses the city, the Indemnity in low orbit goes with it. Three hundred and eighty-four people in chains. Sixty-one of them children." She names the manifest count from P1 S3 verbatim. She does not pose it as a question this time. There is a beat of comm silence; then Varth, careful again: "Maya. Eyes on the table. We will deal with the ship if we have time." Maya does not respond. The spectator/security PC carrying the Assiduous news to the felt should be told privately: "Maya is not on the Banshee anymore. The Banshee is parked in Bay 9. She left twenty minutes ago. Varth is covering for her on the comm." This is the second of three telegraphs (P1 S3, here, P3 S3 dock-side beat). Players who clock it have a real chance to intervene before the orbital moral choice fires; players who don't will feel the weight when it does. Note in the campaign log.

The Day 2 -> Day 3 transition hands cleanly into adv3-p2-s3 (Pressure Cooker, Day 3 morning Maya/Varth argument). Mandelbrot gavels Day 2 closed at midnight; the bracket narrows to twenty-four players; the surviving PCs advance to the Day 3 morning beat.

=== JAM-CAPABILITY DIALOGUE UPGRADE (P3 S5 EARN-IN) ===
Right after Tell #2, Maya and Varth have an explicit, intelligence-driven exchange about the orbital options. Maya names the *Assiduous*'s EW capability against slave-circuit bands. Varth confirms it and names the only unjammable path — bridge override panel, hard-line, physically aboard the *Indemnity*. Maya understands and goes silent. **THIS DIALOGUE EARNS THE P3 S5 SKIRMISH JAMMING.** Without it, the Operator-lane diminishing-returns mechanic in the orbital scene reads as GM fiat. With it, the players know exactly why the lane is closing as the Star Destroyer closes range — they were warned, in plain sight, by the two NPCs who would know.

Varth's role here is critical: he gives Maya the tactical truth and then declines to offer a plan. He hands her the only working path and lets her carry the cost. This is the most surgical version of his Adv3 betrayal — operational truth delivered with no operational support. He knows the second Maya understands the firmware path, she has already made the decision. He chooses not to flag it.

Players who clock this dialogue should be told privately (Insight Resist 3): "Varth gave her the answer. He did not give her a way back."

scenes.title: The Pressure Cooker
scenes.subtitle: Day 3
scenes.readAloud:
Before the tables open on Day 3, you catch Maya and Varth in a hushed argument near the docking bay. Maya's voice is low but furious:

"There are people on that ship, Varth. Living people in slave circuits. We have the datapad. We know where the Indemnity docks. We could —"

Varth cuts her off, cold and final: "That is not why we are here. We are here for the money. A rescue operation against an Imperial slave transport is suicide, and I will not risk this crew on your conscience."

Maya stares at him. Then she walks away without another word.

Day three. Only two tables remain. The buy-ins have escalated, and the audience has shifted from celebration to funeral silence.

Midway through the session, a Devaronian gambler named Szygar goes bust against Arandis. He snaps, leaping up and screaming accusations of cheating. A hold-out blaster appears in his hand.

Panic ripples through the crowd. Arandis doesn't flinch.
scenes.gmNotes:
OPENING BEAT: The heroes overhear Maya and Varth arguing about the Indemnity slave transport (from the Trandoshan datapad in Part 1). Maya wants to intervene and free the slaves. Varth shuts her down — too risky, not the mission. This is critical foreshadowing: Maya cares enough to act. When she later goes to the slave ship on her own and Varth conveniently never tells the crew, the players will remember this moment and understand what he allowed to happen.

The Szygar incident is a test for the heroes. If working security, they must subdue him without causing a casino shutdown. If playing, they must decide whether to intervene. If heroes don't act, Arandis's undercover Stormtroopers will vaporize Szygar, potentially causing a police investigation that cancels the tournament. Varth: 'Don't let them shoot! If the cops shut us down, we lose the money!' Success earns trust from casino owner Jacc Mandelbrot.

scenes.title: The Final Table
scenes.subtitle: Day 4
scenes.readAloud:
The final day. Five players remain under a harsh spotlight: Arandis, Fioro, Draver, the Rodian Creeska, and you.

Arandis plays strangely — folding strong hands against everyone except Fioro. He goes All In against her. She calls.

He reveals a losing hand. The crowd erupts.

But Arandis isn't sweeping his cards away. His left hand drifts, casually, to brush his earpiece — the small private gesture of a man transmitting a confirmation. Then, with deliberate ceremony — three slow taps, one card per tap — he lays them out face-up across the felt in a row, dead-center where the gallery cameras can see them: One of Coins. Three of Sabers. Seven of Flasks.

At Fioro's shoulder her bodyguard exhales — a small, audible release of held breath. Fioro herself does not react at all, which is the loudest reaction in the room.

Varth's voice cuts in over the spectator/security side-band — the Competitor PC's pin is still jamming, so they hear nothing yet:

"1-3-7. That's a frequency — 137.12. It's the slave circuit control code for the Indemnity. He just handed her the keys to the getaway car AND the money. Get that to whoever's at the table. NOW."
scenes.gmNotes:
The climax of the tournament. The tournament's REAL job — and the only thing that matters at this table — is for the crew to (a) confirm Lady Fioro is Varga's proxy and (b) get a fix on Varga's hideout via her movements after the Final Table. Pot outcome is flavor. The wafer/137.12 frequency is a tactical asset, not a campaign gate (Maya doesn't need it for the Indemnity; the crew doesn't need it to find Varga).

THE THREE TELLS BEFORE VARTH'S DECODE — give attentive players a chance to call it themselves. The new read-aloud now front-loads three in-fiction tells BEFORE Varth's voice-over:
• ARANDIS'S EARPIECE TOUCH (PRE-CARDS) — a confirming hand-to-ear gesture. Insight Resist 3 reads it as a transmit-confirmation, not a nervous tic. A spectator/security PC who calls it out gets to ask Mandelbrot whether anyone is on the tournament's licensed comm channels — Mandelbrot confirms a second, unlicensed channel just lit up.
• THE CEREMONIAL CARD PLACEMENT (THREE TAPS, DEAD-CENTER, GALLERY-FACING) — a deliberate display, not a sweep. Insight Resist 2 (one tier easier — this is the loudest tell) reads it as a coded transmission to someone watching, not a humiliated loser making a point.
• FIORO'S BODYGUARD'S EXHALE + FIORO'S NON-REACTION — Insight Resist 3 reads the bodyguard as relieved that an expected signal landed, and Fioro's stillness as the practiced calm of a courier who just received the package. A PC who clocks this AND the earpiece tell auto-IDs Fioro as the proxy without needing Varth's decode.
A PC who reads any one tell may attempt the decode themselves at Resist 4 (Wits/calculation): success = 1-3-7-12, slave circuit frequency, before Varth says it. Reward player attention. Varth's decode then becomes confirmation, not revelation, which makes the table feel sharp instead of led.

[CANONICAL PATH — the card-arrangement happens.] Arandis deliberately loses the massive pot to Fioro, transferring the Imperial payment. The card arrangement is a code — the slave circuit frequency for the Indemnity (137.12). Fioro now has the credits (digitally transferred to a datapad) and the ship code. Varth decodes 137.12 in real time (or confirms a PC's earlier decode). Whether the crew interferes with the pot, lets it pass, or sits idle, Fioro stands up to leave with what looks like the keys to Varga's getaway. THE CREW MUST ACT — either grab her in the Draver heist crossfire (adv3-p2-s5) or tail her quietly to Docking Bay 4414. Either way the next move is the assault on Varga.

[FLAVOR VARIATION — Switch's Dirty Money in play.] If a PC took Switch's contract and the crew is actively helping Moro win, Moro takes the Final Table pot and the wafer never reaches Fioro. Switch pays the crew 5-7% of Moro's pot. Fioro is STILL identifiable as Varga's proxy from her bodyguard rotation, her seat-side comms with Arandis between hands, and the way Arandis tried to feed her — the table-read still works. The crew loses the 137.12 tactical asset (Maya works around it via her dock-crew contacts) but keeps the Varga lead. Mandelbrot Rapport may shift depending on whether the crew's table-side cheating got noticed (skulduggery vs Resist 4 — failure = expulsion).

[FAILURE MODE — DO NOT LET THE TABLE DRIFT HERE.] If the crew somehow lets Fioro walk untailed AND uncaptured AND unobserved, Varga collects the payday and disappears. That breaks the campaign — Adv3's mandatory outcome is Varga's death and the implant recovery. Mandelbrot, Maya, and Varth all push hard for the strike; Fyren's Ugnaughts can volunteer a tail; if every PC stalls, the GM should have Fioro's bodyguard make a clumsy comm call that names the docking bay aloud.

Wire the proxy ID and the Docking Bay 4414 fix through to adv3-p3-s1 (Gauntlet). The assault on Varga is what triggers Imperial cleanup, which is what puts the gas hauler on collision course with the Indemnity in adv3-p3-s5. That orbital climax fires regardless of Switch/Moro flavor.

scenes.subtitle: Combat
scenes.readAloud:
Just as you move to intercept Fioro, Silas Draver makes his play. He stands, pulls a heavy blaster, and fires into the ceiling.

"Nobody moves! The Empire isn't the only one getting paid today!"

The dealer droids spin around, revealing hidden blaster cannons. Draver's men — disguised as waiters and guests — pull weapons and secure the exits. Draver grabs Fioro, pressing a blaster to her temple.

"The datapad. Now."
scenes.gmNotes:
[OUTCOME GATE — wire from adv3-p2-s4 (Final Table).]
  [OUTCOME A — IMPERIAL FORK (default).] Fioro won the Final Table; Arandis transfers the wafer (137.12 The Indemnity frequency) to her datapad. Draver heists the casino to take Fioro hostage and seize that wafer. This scene runs as written — Fioro is the hostage, the datapad on the felt holds the Indemnity intel, and beat 4 confirms the wafer.
  [OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK.] Moro won the Final Table. No wafer transferred (Arandis aborted the payment). Draver's heist STILL fires — he has been planning this for months and isn't going to walk away — but his hostage is now MORO (the upset winner), and the "datapad" he wants is Moro's chip rack (which represents the Switch payout the crew is owed). Where this scene's text references "Fioro," "the wafer," "the 137.12 frequency," or "Indemnity intel," substitute "Moro," "the chip rack," and "the Switch payout chips." Beat 4's confirmation check becomes "extracting Moro alive WITH the chip rack" instead of "confirming the wafer." Arandis still dies in the crossfire (his death is canon and important regardless of fork — he has seen the crew's faces and knows them as players in the tournament). The Docking Bay 4414 intel that Fioro spills in beat 4 ALSO surfaces under Outcome B — but from a different source: Moro, terrified after the hostage rescue, mentions overhearing Varga's couriers talking about "4414" in the bathhouse the night before. Same handoff to adv3-p2-s6.

  Three-way crossfire in a crowded casino. Draver weaponized the dealer droids and planted his men as staff. The heroes are caught between Draver's heist crew, panicking civilians, and Arandis who draws a concealed military blaster to protect the transaction's secrecy. Arandis likely dies in the crossfire, removing the Imperial witness. Varth: 'Forget the civilians! Get the datapad!' After defeating Draver, Fioro spills Varga's location: Docking Bay 4414.

beats.title: Draver's Reveal
beats.readAloud:
Silas Draver does not look like a man about to do what he is about to do. He stands slowly, almost amused, like he is calling for a drink. The blaster he produces from inside his coat is not amused. It is a heavy military sidearm, the kind a man buys when he plans to use it.

He fires once into the chandelier. Crystal rains. The room screams.

'Nobody moves! The Empire isn't the only one getting paid today!'

Four figures who were waiters thirty seconds ago pull weapons from under jackets and aprons. The dealer droids spin a quarter-turn to reveal blaster cannons concealed in their torsos. Draver crosses to Lady Fioro in three long strides, locks an arm around her throat, and presses the muzzle of the heavy blaster against her temple.

'The datapad. Now.'

INCITING BEAT — Draver weaponizes the room. Establish three things in this beat:
• Draver has been planning this for the entire tournament. His 'drunk gambler' cover is a months-long con.
• The dealer droids are not casino property anymore — they're Draver's. He bought a slicer access to the casino's droid maintenance pipeline three weeks ago.
• Fioro is the hostage AND the target. Draver wants the wafer in her datapad as much as Varga's people do.

INITIATIVE NOTE: Draver acts BEFORE the crew on the surprise round. The dealer droids act on his initiative. The four disguised thugs act one slot later. The crew rolls initiative starting on round 1 of the actual fight.

IF A PC HAS A LINE-OF-FIRE ON DRAVER IMMEDIATELY: they may attempt a snap shot before initiative resolves. Resist 5 (Draver is using Fioro as cover, the crowd is screaming, the lighting just changed). Success = Draver takes Fleeting damage but does NOT release Fioro; he uses Snap Shot to return fire on the same PC at -2 Power. Failure = the round proceeds normally. This is the moment for a Pilot or Skulduggery PC to feel cinematic.

beats.title: The Three-Way Crossfire
beats.readAloud: Arandis is on his feet before the crystal hits the floor. The Imperial Bagman pulls a compact military blaster from a shoulder rig — sleeker than his civilian cover suggested, regulation issue, the kind a man carries when his real employer is a ministry. He fires twice across the table, dropping one of Draver's thugs. Then he pivots toward Fioro and the wafer in her datapad. He does not seem to notice the crew. He is doing his job.
beats.gmNotes:
FACTION GEOMETRY — three sides on the floor, plus civilians.

FACTION 1: THE CREW. Their goal is the datapad. Secondary goals: keep Fioro alive (she has the Docking Bay 4414 intel for s6), survive the Imperial witness, get out before Wing Guard arrives.
FACTION 2: DRAVER + 4 THUGS + 2 DEALER DROIDS. Goal: take the datapad and exfiltrate via the kitchen back-corridor (Draver's pre-planned escape). Will kill Fioro if cornered.
FACTION 3: ARANDIS + 2 IMPERIAL PLAINCLOTHES (concealed in the gallery — bring out as needed if the table is large enough for the threat). Goal: secure the datapad for the Empire and eliminate any witness who saw the card transmission. ARANDIS DOES NOT RECOGNIZE THE CREW AS A FACTION YET — he treats them as crossfire, not enemies, unless they actively engage him.
FACTION 4 (NON-COMBATANT): ~80 panicking civilians, Mandelbrot's house security (4 unarmed bouncers + 2 armed pit bosses, defending the cashier's vault not the floor), the press credentials and tournament gallery.

FACTION-INTERACTION RULES:
• Draver vs Arandis is the priority pair — they will shoot each other before they shoot the crew, IF the crew is not actively interfering. Smart PCs can let the two factions tire each other out.
• If a PC deliberately engages Arandis, he reclassifies them as hostile and brings his concealed support up to bear. This is a real cost — Arandis is a Tier 2 Harrier and his support are professionals.
• If a PC deliberately engages Draver, his thugs and the dealer droids prioritize that PC.
• If a PC tries to grab Fioro from Draver: opposed Physique vs Draver's Reflex. Success = Fioro free, Draver takes Fleeting damage from the wrench, both PC and Draver are now in the same zone. Failure = Draver pivots, blaster comes off Fioro's temple onto the PC's, and Draver becomes a Snap Shot threat.

ARANDIS DEATH BEAT: in normal play, Arandis catches a stray bolt from one of Draver's thugs (or Draver himself) sometime in round 2-3. Make this CINEMATICALLY OBVIOUS — he stumbles, looks down at the smoking hole in his uniform, and his last words are clipped Imperial protocol: 'Field office... compromised... transmit...' before he goes down. The Imperial witness to the card transmission is now dead — the crew will not be hunted by ISB for what they saw. This is a deliberate and important narrative outcome. Do not let Arandis survive past round 4.

beats.title: The Civilian Problem
beats.readAloud:
Eighty-some patrons are screaming, ducking, climbing over tables. A Sullustan in formal wear is hyperventilating under a roulette table. A human family — a man, a woman, a child no older than eight — is huddled behind an overturned drinks cart twelve meters from Draver. Varth's voice cuts in over comms, sharp and tactical:

'Forget the civilians. Get the datapad. The Wing Guard will sort the bystanders.'
beats.gmNotes:
MORAL/TACTICAL TENSION BEAT — Varth's order is correct on the mission terms and wrong on the human terms. The crew has agency.

VARTH'S ORDER IS NOT A RAILROAD. Players who ignore it and prioritize civilians do not lose the mission — but they pay a tactical cost (turns spent shielding civilians = turns Draver gains on the datapad).

MECHANICAL OPTIONS FOR THE CIVILIAN-CARING PC:
• HERDING THE CROWD: Charm or Presence (Resist 3) to direct one cluster of ~10 civilians to the kitchen exit. Costs the PC's action for the round.
• HUMAN SHIELD POSITIONING: Athletics (Resist 3) to physically place yourself between Draver's line of fire and a civilian cluster. Costs movement, grants no mechanical bonus, but if the GM is tracking Comfort/Reputation with the Cloud City civilian population, this is a Major positive moment that pays in adv3-p3-s2 (Hutt's Hangar) when a Wing Guard sergeant remembers a face from the casino news.
• CALLING FOR HELP: Tech (Resist 3) to slice the casino's emergency PA and direct civilians to the exits. Costs action, but reduces the civilian death count in the GM's narrative reckoning by ~80%.

VARTH'S RED FLAG WATCH: this is NOT a numbered Varth red flag, but it is foreshadowing texture. A PC who is paying attention to Varth as a character will notice that he gave the order without hesitation. Insight (Resist 3) reads it as 'Varth is mission-focused to the point of cold.' Do not narrate this conclusion — let the player draw it.

IF THE CREW IGNORES THE CIVILIANS ENTIRELY: 6-12 die in the crossfire. Cloud City public opinion turns against the crew. Wing Guard pursuit in P3 S1 (Gauntlet) is more aggressive. Adv4+ groundwork: word reaches Maz Kanata at Takodana about the casino massacre, and her welcome at the payday hand-off in P3 S6 is colder.

IF THE CREW SAVES THE FAMILY (the human cluster behind the drinks cart specifically): plant the father's name as 'Avor Renn, Cloud City freight handler.' He becomes a recurring civilian contact for any Bespin return visits in the mid-campaign.

beats.title: Securing the Datapad
beats.readAloud: Draver's grip on Fioro slips as he takes the killing shot. He drops to one knee, his blaster spinning out of his hand across the marble. Fioro slumps free. The datapad — a flat black slab the size of a deck of cards — sits in plain view on the felt where Arandis's losing hand still lies.
beats.gmNotes:
WIN-CONDITION BEAT — Draver falls, Fioro is wounded but alive, the datapad is exposed. The crew's job in this beat is to GRAB IT and CONFIRM IT before Wing Guard arrives.

GRABBING THE DATAPAD: free action for any PC adjacent to the table.

CONFIRMING THE DATAPAD HAS THE WAFER (and the wafer has the 137.12 frequency): Tech check Resist 3, takes one round of action time. Success = confirmed, data integrity intact, ready to feed into adv3-p2-s6 and the Indemnity intercept. Masterful = the PC also extracts the bagman authentication chain that Arandis used, which is mildly useful as a future ISB-impersonation tool. Legendary = the PC also cracks the wafer's secondary partition, which contains a list of every Imperial proxy Arandis has paid in the last 18 months — campaign-meaningful intel that Switch will pay 8,000 credits for in adv4.

FAILURE STATE: if the PC botches the Tech check, the datapad is intact but the wafer's encryption seizes. Maya can recover it by hand on the Banshee in flight (no campaign loss, just a 30-minute downtime delay).

FIORO'S CONDITION: she is wounded (one of Draver's bolts caught her shoulder during the hostage struggle). Conscious. Terrified. Talkative. She will spill her guts in adv3-p2-s6 — but only IF the crew keeps her alive for it. If a PC executes her in the heat of the moment (rare but possible), the Docking Bay 4414 intel still surfaces from Varth's data sweep but is delayed by 4 minutes — narratively this means the crew arrives at the hangar to find Varga already aboard the Glorious Chariot with engines hot, and the assault becomes a starship boarding action instead of a hangar fight. NOT a campaign break — but it changes the texture of the climax.

WING GUARD ARRIVAL: 90 seconds out. Sirens audible. The crew has time to grab the datapad, drag Fioro to her feet, and exfiltrate via the south kitchen corridor (the same one Draver was planning to use). Hand off to adv3-p2-s6 (The Aftermath) the moment the crew clears the casino floor.

OUTCOME B (DIRTY MONEY FORK) ADAPTATION: substitute Moro for Fioro and the chip rack for the datapad throughout this beat. The "confirm the wafer" Tech check becomes a Skulduggery Resist 3 to verify the chip count is genuine (Switch will not pay on counterfeit chips). Same DCs, same scaling. Moro is wounded but conscious — his Docking Bay 4414 mention is delivered while Maya patches him on the kitchen-corridor extraction. The narrative ARRIVES AT THE SAME HANDOFF as Outcome A; only the prize and the intel-source differ.

scenes.title: The Aftermath
scenes.readAloud:
The casino is a wreck. Sirens wail in the distance. Lady Fioro, wounded and terrified, spills everything.

"He's at the lower docks — Docking Bay 4414. He has the Indemnity holding in orbit on slave circuits. He's taking the gas and the slaves and leaving the sector tonight!"

Varth scans the system. His voice is grim: "The Indemnity just activated its engines. And... damn it. The Assiduous just entered the system. Draco is here. Get to the hangar. If Varga launches, we lose everything."
scenes.gmNotes:
Fioro reveals Varga's location and the Indemnity's status. Varth confirms Draco has entered the system. The heroes must flee the crime scene and race through Cloud City to the industrial docks before Varga escapes. This is a transition scene — setting up Part 3.

=== MAKE THE ASSAULT THE WANTED PLAY, NOT THE FORCED PLAY ===

This is the moment the crew commits to the hangar assault. The bible declares the assault canonical (walking away = campaign failure), but the GM's job here is to make the assault the OBVIOUS, EAGER choice — never the forced one. If a player ever has to be told 'you can't negotiate,' the agency illusion that holds the campaign together breaks. Stack the table so they WANT to go.

FOUR CONVERGING PUSHES — DELIVER ALL OF THEM IN THIS SCENE:

1) MAYA'S MORAL PUSH (the personal one). Maya cuts in on the open channel as soon as Fioro names the Indemnity: "He's not just leaving. He's taking three hundred and eighty-four people with him. Sixty-one of them children. If he lifts off, that ship goes wherever Varga goes." This is NOT a new Indemnity tell — this is Maya CASHING IN the two tells she has already planted (P1 S3 manifest aside, P2 S2 open-channel recite). Her third and final tell still comes at P3 S3 as the last-chance intervention. Players who tracked the earlier tells feel the weight here; players who didn't get hit with the math now. Maya is not asking. She is stating the count.

2) MANDELBROT'S TACTICAL PUSH (the professional one). Mandelbrot, calm: "Window's eight minutes. Wing Guard's still bought, but Varga's payroll runs out at the dock turnover at midnight. After that the bay's clean and the corridors close. We hit now or we hunt him for two years." A Mandelbrot push — competent, low-emotion, time-bounded — gives tactical PCs a reason to lean in.

3) VARTH'S CLOSURE PUSH (the contractual one). Varth, after Mandelbrot: "The implant walks with him in eight minutes. We came for the implant. The implant is the payday. Anything else is a different conversation we don't have time for tonight." He is correct on the mission terms. Players who took the contract at face value have their reason.

4) THE ASSIDUOUS CLOCK (the existential one). Varth, last: "And the Assiduous can glass the city if Draco decides Varga's a loose end. We do this in eight minutes or we don't do it at all." The Inquisitor is the wall behind every other consideration.

GM RULE: NEVER SAY 'YOU HAVE TO.' If a PC genuinely floats negotiation, walking away, or a slow-play option, do NOT block it. Instead, have one of the four NPCs above answer in-character with the COST of that path: Maya names the slaves who burn, Mandelbrot names the two-year hunt, Varth names the lost payday, the clock names the Inquisitor. Let the PLAYER decide. Almost every player will choose to assault — the four pushes are designed to make assault the obvious moral, tactical, contractual, and survival answer simultaneously. The handful of tables that still walk away can be steered with a final push on the next session — Mandelbrot returning with intelligence that Varga has put a kill-bounty on the crew, retroactively making the assault the safer play.

WHAT IF THEY STILL WALK? Per the bible, this assault is the ONLY viable play — walking away is a campaign-level failure, NOT an equivalent alternate path. Do NOT invent a parallel chase that delivers the same payday. If the table genuinely refuses after all four pushes, end the session there. Open the next session with escalating NPC pressure: Mandelbrot calmly notes the implant has left the system, Switch reports Varga has put a kill-bounty on the crew, Fyren confirms the Wing Guard has flipped from bought to actively hunting, and Varth begins quietly disengaging financially (a soft signal that the contract is dying). Re-offer the assault as a delayed strike — Varga's ship is now in the Outer Rim, the operation is harder, costlier, and the slaves on the Indemnity are days closer to their destination. The path forward is still the assault, just at compounded cost. The Lead Cascade can survive a one-session detour, but it cannot survive the assault never happening.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — The Casino in Ruins
encounters.trigger: Immediately after the s4 heist resolution
encounters.description: The Royal Casino floor is a wreck. Smoke from a discharged blaster hangs in the upper rafters. Two croupier droids are face-down. A Twi'lek dealer is trying to comfort a sobbing Bothan player. Sirens — Wing Guard responding — are audible from the upper concourse and closing fast. Lady Fioro is on the floor against the cashier counter, wounded in the thigh, blood pooling, terrified. She is talking. She will not stop talking. The crew has perhaps four minutes before Wing Guard arrives in force.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — orientation. Establish urgency through ambient detail (the sirens, the Bothan crying, the smoke). Players orient themselves and choose a direction — Fioro is the obvious draw but PCs may also want to grab the wafer from the cashier counter if it was not yet taken in s4. End beat when a PC kneels beside Fioro to listen.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Fioro Spills
encounters.trigger: PC engages with Fioro
encounters.description: Fioro, frightened and bleeding, gives up everything in a rush: "He's at the lower docks — Docking Bay 4414. He has the Indemnity holding in orbit on slave circuits. He's taking the gas and the slaves and leaving the sector tonight! I was supposed to be on that ship. He promised me passage. He is not going to keep that promise. Get him. Get him for me." She thrusts her data-bracelet at the nearest PC — it contains the bay's service-entry codes she was supposed to use to board.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — Fioro talks willingly, terrified by the shooting and abandoned by Varga. Insight check (free) on Fioro: she is telling the truth and she is also planning to vanish off-world the moment Wing Guard distracts the crew. Players may choose to detain her (Wing Guard will find her, she will be charged, she will testify against Varga) or to let her run (she vanishes from the campaign — possibly returning later as a Hapan noble plot in a sequel). The data-bracelet is the deliverable either way.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Varth's Grim Update
encounters.trigger: On the comm, in parallel with Fioro
encounters.description: Varth's voice cuts through the cashier-counter chaos: "The Indemnity just activated its engines. Ten minutes to launch window. And — damn it. The Assiduous has moved. Geosynchronous over Cloud City. Not over the docks. Over the city. Draco is positioning to sterilize if Varga gets clear. We have ten minutes to put hands on Varga or this whole platform is glass." A beat. "Maya is spinning the Banshee up. We have an exit. We do not have a city after this. Move."
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — stakes escalation. Varth's update lands the actual cost of failure: Cloud City's population — millions — is leverage now. The ten-minute clock from this beat carries through s2-s3 (next adventure scenes). Players who heard the Storyteller's "the cost of the gift" or Krygg's Nuvo story should feel the moral weight of "we leave or millions burn" landing on the same nerve.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Out the Service Corridor
encounters.trigger: Wing Guard reaches the casino floor
encounters.description: The crew runs. The casino service corridor — accessible via the Ugnaught keycard if it was earned in adv3-p1-s2 — empties into the lower platform tram station. From there it is six minutes to the lower industrial docks and Bay 4414. Without the keycard, the crew has to fight or talk past two Wing Guard checkpoints, costing two minutes of their ten-minute window. With the Ugnaught safe-house promise from Beat 4 of the s2 conversation, they may stash any wounded crew at the level 312 cantina and pick them up after — Krygg is there cooking the meal he promised.
encounters.tactics: RUN: Stealth / Athletics / fast-talk depending on route. With keycard: clean run, six minutes to docks. Without keycard: 2 checkpoints (Resist 2 each) and a +2 minute penalty per failed check. With safe-house: wounded PCs evacuate to level 312 and continue the next adventure with Krygg's (bad) hot meal already in their stomachs. End scene at the lower docks tram exit.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Hand-off to Part 3
encounters.trigger: Crew arrives at lower industrial docks tram exit
encounters.description: The crew steps off the tram into the lower industrial docks — sodium-orange light, freight haulers, and Docking Bay 4414 visible four hundred meters across the platform, blast doors half-open, Varga's cargo train already moving toward the Indemnity's loading ramp. The Banshee is in low orbit per Maya's plan, ready to extract on signal. The Assiduous is a black wedge in the upper sky. The clock — eight minutes remaining of the ten Varth named — is on every visible chronometer in the dock yard.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — handoff beat. Establishes the geography for adv3-p3-s1 (The Gauntlet) and the eight-minute remaining clock. Players may take one short prep action here (a final comm to Varth, a quick gear check, a moment with Maya on intercom). End the scene the moment a PC commits to the dock approach. Adventure 3 Part 3 begins.

scenes.title: The Gauntlet
scenes.subtitle: Streets of Cloud City
scenes.readAloud:
The journey to the lower docks is a sprint through a city in lockdown. Varga has bribed the Wing Guard to declare you 'Enemy Saboteurs.'

The chase transitions from pristine white corridors into the steam-filled, rusted catwalks of the Industrial District. Tibanna gas vents hiss, obscuring vision, and the orange glow of the Bespin sunset filters through heavy industrial grates.

Varth hacks door controls from the ship: "Left at the junction! No, the other left! I'm jamming their comms, but I can't stop them from shooting at you. Move!"
scenes.gmNotes:
Running battle through Cloud City. The heroes are pinned down by corrupt Wing Guard and Stormtroopers. This is a chase — stopping to fight every enemy means being overwhelmed. Use the environment: shoot steam pipes to scald pursuers, jump onto moving cargo skiffs, cut through maintenance ducts. Varth acts as 'The Man in the Chair,' hacking door controls.

[OUTCOME GATE — wire from adv3-p2-s4.]

[OUTCOME A — IMPERIAL FORK (default).] The crew is chasing Fioro toward the air-tram with the 137.12 frequency wafer in her datapad. The Indemnity lead is intact and feeds the Part 3 sequence as written. The Wing Guard pursuit is hunting the wafer.

[OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK.] No wafer changed hands. Fioro is still at the casino arguing with Varga's on-floor handler about a payment that never arrived. The crew is instead chasing Moro's payout chips toward the Banshee while Switch confirms the 5-7% transfer en route. The Wing Guard pursuit was scrambled by Varga's payroll regardless — Varga is furious that the Imperial money is gone — so the chase still happens, but the prize is the Switch payout, not the Indemnity intel. Adv3 Part 3 downstream scenes (Hutt's Hangar, Firefight, Grand Theft Starship, Skirmish Over Bespin, The Choice) proceed without the Indemnity lead. The Maya rescue beat in adv3-p3-s5 is REPLACED by a Maya quiet-confirmation that the Indemnity transport is no longer reachable through this lead — the slaves on that ship will require a different operation in a later adventure. Flag this in The Choice (adv3-p3-s6) so Varth's deception about Maya is recolored: he never had to let her go, because the lead never materialized.

scenes.title: Hutt's Hangar
scenes.subtitle: Docking Bay 4414
scenes.readAloud:
You kick open the blast doors to Docking Bay 4414. The cavernous hangar is open to the roiling clouds of Bespin on one side, wind howling through the magnetic field.

At the far north end, framed by heavy durasteel scaffolding, the Glorious Chariot squats in her launch cradle — gold and purple, three thruster housings visible through the scaffold gaps, turbines already cycling with a whine that climbs toward takeoff pitch. Between the two tallest scaffold towers, the yacht's boarding ramp is still down.

Six Z-95 Headhunters line the hangar walls — two along the port side, four along the starboard, nose-out toward the center. The rearmost crimson-trimmed fighter on the starboard line carries a Huttese glyph on the fuselage — Varga's stable. Pilots are already sprinting the open floor toward their cockpits, ladders down, engines cycling. Stacked cargo crates clutter the center of the bay — Trandoshan manifests, Guild Tibanna-gas hazard placards, still warm from the offload.

Varga's voice booms from the cradle's loudspeakers, fat with panic. When a cradle monitor cuts to a live feed, he sees you. Fear becomes rage.

"Kill them! They brought the Inquisitor down on us! I want their heads! Get me in the air NOW!"
scenes.gmNotes:
The final confrontation with Varga. The Glorious Chariot sits in the adjacent launch cradle at the NORTH end of the map, her thrusters visible through the scaffolding, boarding ramp still down between the scaffold towers. Six Z-95 Headhunters line the hangar walls (2 port, 4 starboard) and their pilots are racing the open floor toward cockpits.

THE LAUNCH CLOCK: The Chariot is priming for launch. Track it as 6 beats. Each beat is one round of the fight. When the clock hits zero, the Chariot lifts and the scene transitions into s3 (Firefight — closing the hangar) and then s4/s5 (Grand Theft Starship + Skirmish Over Bespin — pursuit in orbit). The Chariot leaving is a BAD outcome but not a fail state — it's the 'normal' path and the pursuit is the planned finale. Stopping the Chariot before launch is the HARD path.

TWO WIN CONDITIONS, TWO PATHS:
1. STOP THE CHARIOT (hard): Heroes must reach the Launch Cradle zone at the north end before beat 6. Options once there — (a) ascend the ramp and fight Varga aboard the yacht (his bulk is a weapon in the narrow corridors — use the ramp/airlock as a choke point), (b) sabotage the visible thruster housings from the scaffolding (Tech check, Hard — successful disable locks the Chariot on the pad), (c) trigger the Tibanna-gas cargo crates as a chained detonation that cracks the cradle mounts (requires reaching the crates AND igniting them while heroes have already moved north — high risk). If heroes pull any of these off, Varga is trapped — boss fight on his terms, but he can't flee.
2. LET THE CHARIOT LAUNCH (normal): Heroes steal a Z-95 from the walls and chase the yacht into Bespin's atmosphere (s4 → s5). This is the designed through-line. The hangar fight becomes a sprint to a cockpit rather than an assault on the ramp.

PILOT INTERCEPT ECONOMY: Each Z-95 pilot that reaches a cockpit and launches = one additional harrier in s5. Shooting pilots on the ladders is high-value. Make this explicit to the table.

SCAFFOLDING: Climbable with Athletics. Ascending the scaffold opens a sightline to the cradle AND a path to the ramp. BUT when the Chariot's engines reach full cycle (beat 4+), heat wash makes the scaffolding impassable. Audibility in the north half of the hangar drops to zero — shouted coordination fails on beat 4+.

VARGA'S POSITION: On the Chariot's bridge or at the top of the ramp. NOT on the hangar floor. Heroes who want to engage Varga directly MUST climb the scaffolding or push up the ramp. He shouts commands and taunts via the cradle PA; the scene's emotional presence is his voice in the hangar, his physical presence one zone away behind the scaffold.

CARGO CRATE HAZARD: The center-floor crate cluster is Guild-marked Tibanna gas. Sustained fire or a deliberate ignition check triggers an area detonation — [Concealment] smoke wall for 2 beats, damage to anyone adjacent, and if heroes position it right, the blast cracks the cradle mount scaffolding. High-risk, high-reward environmental play.

tacticalMap.gmTacticalNotes:
FOCAL ZONES: Cargo Crates (primary cover cluster), Starboard Fighter Line (four Z-95s including Varga's crimson personal craft), and Hangar Floor (deadly open ground connecting them).

HERO ENTRY: Hangar Entrance (south). The crew rolls in hot from the Gauntlet (s1) and must decide in the first beat: push straight up the floor (fastest, fully exposed), hug the port fighter line (cover but bypassed by starboard fire), or make the cargo crate cluster (primary cover but a pilot scramble race).

VARGA'S PILOTS: Mercenary pilots sprint from the starboard entrance (or were already in the Starboard Fighter Line) toward their Z-95 cockpits. Each Z-95 that launches = one TIE-equivalent harrier in s5 (Skirmish Over Bespin). Grounding pilots on the deck in s2 directly reduces the swarm size in s5. Make this explicit to the table — every shot that drops a scrambling pilot is a fighter that doesn't launch.

VARGA'S PERSONAL Z-95: Rearmost fighter in the Starboard Fighter Line. Crimson detailing, Huttese glyph on fuselage. If heroes want to STEAL a ship for the s4 'Grand Theft Starship' beat, this is the prestige target — fully fueled, hot-swap ready, Varga's own. Alternative: any of the other Z-95s works, but taking Varga's specifically has downstream narrative weight (Varga screams about it on comms, adds +1 to Grief pool in s6).

REAR EXHAUST HAZARD: Rear Exhaust Wall vents cycle every 2 beats. PCs or NPCs in the zone when vents fire take flue-gas damage AND audibility drops to zero — shouted coordination fails for one beat. Good for narrative swings when a pilot tries to reach a Z-95 by running the rear.

CARGO CRATE FIRE RISK: Crates are Guild-marked Tibanna gas. A stray sustained-fire hit OR a deliberate tech/ranged check can ignite one — area explosion, [Concealment] smoke wall for 2 beats, random damage to anyone adjacent. Table should know the crates are volatile before they take cover there. Mercenary fire will eventually ignite them if the fight drags — use this as a clock.

LOCKDOWN PANEL: Hangar Entrance has an emergency lockdown panel. Tech check (Hard) seals the main door. This can SAVE the crew from reinforcements coming in from the concourse — or TRAP them in with whatever is already in the hangar. Hard tradeoff worth offering explicitly.

PATROL GEOMETRY: Port Fighter Line and Starboard Fighter Line cross-fire the open floor. Taking cover in the port line means losing sightlines to the starboard line and vice-versa. Crew either splits the room or commits to one side.

EXIT VECTOR: s4 (Grand Theft Starship) begins the moment a PC reaches a Z-95 cockpit and powers up. If the hangar bay doors are sealed by the lockdown panel, a PC must also hit the external bay-door control (another Tech beat) before liftoff.

scenes.readAloud:
The hangar erupts into chaos. Blaster bolts ricochet off hull plating and fuel crates. The Z-95 engines roar to life one by one. Varga, seeing his mercenaries fall, turns and lumbers up the boarding ramp of the Glorious Chariot.

The yacht's engines begin their warm-up cycle. If he seals that ramp, he's gone.
scenes.gmNotes:
The climactic ground fight. Heroes must cross the hangar using fuel crates and machinery for cover. Primary objective: stop the Glorious Chariot from launching. If Z-95s get airborne, they strafe the hangar floor. If heroes breach the yacht, they fight Varga in opulent but narrow corridors. Varga fights desperately — he knows this is his last stand.

TELEGRAPH MAYA'S OBSESSION — TELL #3 OF 3 (LAST CHANCE TO INTERVENE). At the first lull in the firefight — the moment a PC ducks behind cover to reload, or right after the first Z-95 goes down — a sharp PC's open-channel comm should pick up Maya's voice on a SHIPS-INTERNAL band, not the crew band. Faint, partial, like a comm leaking from a vessel docked nearby: "...auxiliary lock, deck six, manifest hold..." then static. Any PC who calls her on the crew band gets nothing. Varth, if asked directly, hesitates one beat too long and then says: "She is in position. Stay on the Hutt." That is the final tell. A PC who breaks off and runs to a comm station can confirm in 30 seconds that Maya is aboard the Indemnity in low orbit — but doing so means leaving the hangar fight short-handed for one round (give the rest of the crew a -1 to their next Resist while the runner is away). If the crew decides AT THIS MOMENT to abort and extract Maya, the orbital choice in P3 S5 changes shape: they arrive at the Indemnity BEFORE the Imperial gas-hauler does, and the moral choice becomes 'how many can we get off' instead of 'save Maya or jump.' This is the payoff for tracking the P1 S3 and P2 S2 telegraphs. Crews that did not track them, or do not act here, hit the orbital choice as written.

[OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK.] Moro won the Final Table. No wafer transferred. No 137.12 frequency. The chase/firefight/escape still happens (Varga is enraged the Imperial money never landed and his Wing Guard payroll is still pursuing the crew), but the prize at the end of this scene is the Switch payout (5-7% of Moro's pot), NOT Indemnity intel. Where this scene's text references the wafer/frequency/Indemnity, treat those references as the Switch payout chips and Moro's extraction.
