beats.title: The Clock Starts
beats.readAloud:
Varga's body is still cooling when Varth's voice comes over the comm — taut, fast, no ornament:

'Imperial stormtroopers have breached the elevator shaft. You have thirty seconds before a platoon comes through that door. You can't go back the way you came. Take the ships. Steal the yacht. I'll rendezvous with you in orbit. MOVE.'

The elevator shaft begins to thrum. Far down the corridor, you can hear the regular hammer-beat of armored boots accelerating up a service stair.
beats.gmNotes:
30-SECOND HARD CLOCK — this is a literal mechanic. From the moment Varth's order ends, the players have FIVE ROUNDS of in-fiction action before the platoon arrives. Track it visibly: put a token down on the table that says ROUND 5, and remove one each round. Make the count public.

WHAT 'TOO LATE' MEANS: at the end of round 5, if any PC is not aboard a launching ship, the platoon enters the hangar. 20 stormtroopers with disciplined fire and Pinning Barrage. This is a TPK encounter — the npcs[] block notes it explicitly. Players who don't make the clock should feel the bottom drop out.

DO NOT FUDGE THE CLOCK. The whole emotional point of the scene is the cost of the previous fights — every wound, every spent Power pip, every distraction from the previous beats was time they don't have now. If a PC is downed, they need to be dragged onto a ship by another PC (counts as the rescuer's full action).

ALTERNATIVELY (if the GM wants to soften the landing for a struggling table): a Wing Guard sergeant who saw the family-saving in adv3-p2-s5-b3 buys the crew an extra round by misdirecting the platoon's leader at the elevator. This is a one-time use, must be earned, and should be played as the universe paying back a moral debt — not as a freebie.

beats.title: Choosing Ships
beats.readAloud: The hangar holds three flyable craft: the Glorious Chariot, Varga's personal yacht — luxurious, armored, big enough for the whole crew but slow off the deck. Two Z-95 Headhunters in launch cradles along the south wall — older Clone Wars-era fighters, fast, mean, single-pilot, wired and prepped for immediate launch (Varga kept them as escort hot-standby). And a battered repair skiff against the back, marked with Mandelbrot's company chevron — almost certainly his courier vehicle.
beats.gmNotes:
TACTICAL CHOICE BEAT — the existing decisionPoints[] block frames this. Players pick the mix that matches their crew composition.

SHIP TRADEOFFS (use these to inform the table):
• THE GLORIOUS CHARIOT (luxury yacht): seats 8 comfortably, decent shields, twin medium turrets, hyperdrive Class 2. PRIMARY ESCAPE VEHICLE. One PC pilots; one PC mans the dorsal turret. Other PCs are passengers (or one mans a secondary station). Disadvantage: it is BIG and SLOW off the launch pad; takes a full round of pre-launch warmup. Advantage: in the orbital scrum (adv3-p3-s5), it can absorb hits the Headhunters cannot.
• Z-95 HEADHUNTERS (×2): single-seat, fast, agile, twin laser cannons + 2 concussion missiles. PRE-WARMED — can launch in half a round. Best for any PC with the Pilot vocation or Ace destiny. The Headhunters significantly improve the crew's survival odds in adv3-p3-s5 by occupying TIE pursuit.
• MANDELBROT'S SKIFF: not flyable for orbital combat (no hyperdrive, atmosphere-only). However, it is rigged with Mandelbrot's tournament-administrator credentials and CAN punch through the Wing Guard cordon at the lower-city dock without a fight. Useful escape option for any PC who is wounded or who needs to extract a non-combatant (Fioro? Maya, if not aboard the Banshee?). Mandelbrot will not be furious if it's borrowed; he keeps three.

SPLIT-CREW RULE: the crew can split across multiple craft. The Chariot needs at least one pilot. Z-95s each need a dedicated pilot. The skiff is autopilot-capable.

IF THE CREW HAS NO PILOT VOCATION OR ACE DESTINY: the Z-95s are still flyable, but at -2 Power on all piloting checks. Strongly suggest the GM nudge the table toward Chariot-only in this case.

beats.title: Boarding & Hot Start
beats.readAloud: The deck plates ring under your boots. The Chariot's boarding ramp is already cycling open — Varga left the launch sequence on standby, expecting a quick exit. The Z-95s' canopies hiss back the moment a hand touches the cradle release. Whatever you are taking, whatever you are leaving, you are doing it in the next ten seconds.
beats.gmNotes:
EXECUTION BEAT — three parallel streams happen simultaneously. Cut between them rapidly, heist-movie style. ~30 seconds of real-world table time per stream.

STREAM A — CHARIOT PILOT: Tech or Piloting check Resist 3 to spin up the engines while running. Success = ship is hot at end of beat, ready to launch. Failure = one extra round of warmup needed, eats into the platoon clock.

STREAM B — CHARIOT TURRET / SECONDARY STATION: free action to mount the turret. The dorsal cannon is fire-ready the moment the bay doors open in beat 4.

STREAM C — Z-95 PILOTS: Athletics check Resist 2 to vault into the cradle and seal the canopy in time. Success = launch on next round. Failure (rare) = the cradle release sticks and the PC loses one round trying to override; if they fail the override Tech Resist 3, they must abandon the Z-95 and run for the Chariot ramp.

WOUNDED OR DOWNED PCs: must be carried by another PC (carrier loses their action for the round). Drag-to-Chariot ramp is the priority — the Chariot can carry passengers, the Z-95s cannot.

FIORO (if alive and brought along from p2-s6): she's terrified but cooperative. She rides in the Chariot. She'll need to be sedated or strapped in — Maya handles this if Maya is aboard, otherwise it costs a PC half an action.

MAYA'S LOCATION: Maya and the Banshee are NOT in this hangar. They're at the dock with the Banshee, holding orbital position over Cloud City. The crew rendezvouses with the Banshee in adv3-p3-s5. Make sure the table understands the Chariot/Z-95s are an EXIT vector, not a permanent ride.

MANDELBROT'S LOCATION: Mandelbrot is back at the casino managing the post-incident press. He'll meet the crew at the Takodana payday.

beats.title: The Launch
beats.readAloud:
The hangar door at the south end of the bay is locked down — Varga's standing security protocol, default-closed. The Stormtroopers' boots are loud now, just past the elevator. You hear a voice on the other side of the corridor door bark a Republic-era breach code, and the door's lock LED flashes from green to amber.

The pilot in the Chariot's command chair sees the manual override switch under a glass cover, marked in Huttese: BURN THROUGH. Nothing subtle about it.
beats.gmNotes:
FINAL EXIT BEAT — the hangar door must be opened or the ships are trapped. Two methods.

METHOD 1 — BURN THROUGH (default, dramatic). The Chariot pilot flips the BURN THROUGH cover and fires the dorsal cannon at the closed hangar door. The door blows outward in a ruined gout of slag. Pros: fast, free, instantly clears the route. Cons: the explosion alerts every Imperial gunnery station within range, contributing one [Tracking Lock] condition to the Chariot at the start of adv3-p3-s5. ALSO: if any PC has lingering Wing Guard sympathy from beat 3, this is a brutal way to leave their last memory of the city — burning a hole through it.

METHOD 2 — SLICE THE LOCK (Tech, Resist 4). Quieter, no [Tracking Lock]. Costs one round of action time. Success = door rolls open clean. Failure = burn through is the fallback. Masterful = the slice ALSO blocks the corridor door behind the Stormtroopers for one round, buying breathing room.

LAUNCH SEQUENCE (round 5, end of clock): all ships punch atmosphere together. The Chariot leads, Z-95s on its wings. Cloud City's industrial-district skyline drops away in seconds. The orange of Bespin sunset gives way to the upper haze, then the indigo edge of atmosphere, then black. Hand off DIRECTLY to adv3-p3-s5 (Skirmish Over Bespin) — the Assiduous is in orbit, the Banshee is hailing on a tight beam, and the Indemnity's slave-circuit profile is now visible on long-range sensors.

IF THE CREW IS LATE (post-round 5): the Stormtrooper platoon enters the hangar. 20 minions with Disciplined Fire and Pinning Barrage. The Chariot can soak some hits while launching but every PC outside it takes 1 Fleeting damage per round of exposure. 3+ rounds of exposure = TPK risk. The clock is the clock.

scenes.title: Skirmish Over Bespin
scenes.readAloud:
You break atmosphere in stolen ships and the orbital plot lights up like a kicked hive. The Imperial Star Destroyer *Assiduous* hangs in high orbit, launching a wing of TIEs. Below them, *The Indemnity* — three hundred and eighty-four people in chains — drifts on dead reactors, her slave-circuit lockdown showing on every scanner you have. Burning hard on a parabolic intercept is the same automated Tibanna gas hauler your team flagged on Refinery Platform 13 — unmanned, redirected from an Imperial nav-relay, on a clean kinetic vector to scrub the slave-trade evidence.

Your formation: the *Banshee* is already in the slot above you with Varth at her stick (Maya gave him the keys before she went silent). You ride out of the Cloud City cradle in the *Glorious Chariot* with a PC in every station, and any pilots who cracked a Z-95 cockpit during the hangar fight ride wing in single-seat Headhunters. Three hulls on the line. Two minutes on the clock.

Varth's voice, the one that means he has already done the math:

"Spool the hyperdrives. The Hauler is going to impact in under two minutes. We have what we came for. It is a tragedy. It is not our tragedy. Set coordinates and jump."

Then the open-channel cuts in. Maya, breathing hard, comm-leak background of slave-circuit klaxons:

"Varth. I'm on the bridge of the *Indemnity*. The locks won't open from the panel — Imperial firmware rewrote the override handshake. Where is that backup code?"
scenes.gmNotes:
ACT-ONE MORAL CLIMAX. This scene is intentionally **scaffolded as narrative** — the starship-combat engine is wired in (button on the dashboard) but the fight itself is meant to be RUN as a structured narrative skirmish on a 5-round dramatic clock, with optional dice resolution at the GM's table.

=== STAGE / SHIPS ===
• *The Indemnity* — Scale-3 Starship, slave-bulk transport, dead in space, slave circuits locked by Imperial firmware. Maya is on her bridge.
• Tibanna Gas Hauler — Scale-3 Starship, automated, no crew, on a kinetic intercept. Cannot be hailed, can only be destroyed or deflected. The Empire is using it as a kinetic kill weapon.
• *Glorious Chariot* (PC ship, just stolen) — Scale-2 multi-station yacht. Pilot, Gunner(s), Operator, Engineer. PCs distribute themselves at the start of the scene.
• *Banshee* (Varth at the stick) — Scale-2 multi-station freighter, light combat fit. Varth flies this scene; he is functionally a fourth NPC ship, hostile to the Hauler, neutral to TIEs unless pressed.
• Z-95 Headhunters — Scale-1 single-pilot fighters, however many PCs cracked a cockpit in P3 S3. Each one is a single-PC ship.
• TIE Fighter Wing (8) — Scale-1 minions screening the Hauler. Already statted in this scene's NPC block.

=== INITIATIVE ===
Initiative works **identically to character combat** — see the gamesystem 'starship_combat' note. Every PC rolls Tactics (Wits) Join Battle as their personal slot, and every enemy ship gets one slot (NPC static initiative = Tier + Wits×2). One slot per PC, one slot per enemy hull. Multi-station ships share their crew across their slots — the Pilot acts on the Pilot's slot, the Gunner acts on the Gunner's slot, etc.; functionally each PC keeps their own turn. Maya gets her own slot; she is acting on the *Indemnity*'s bridge in parallel.

=== THE 5-ROUND DRAMATIC CLOCK ===
The Hauler will impact at the end of Round 5 unless its drive section is destroyed or its course is broken. The GM may dial the clock to +1 (six rounds, easier) or -1 (four rounds, brutal) based on table tension. Each round, narrate one tick of the impact countdown.

=== THE OPERATOR–CHARIOT JAMMING LANE (DIMINISHING RETURNS) ===
If the crew recovered the 137.12 frequency from the Final Table (Outcome A — Imperial Fork), the Chariot's Operator can attempt to broadcast the slave-circuit override remotely from orbit, freeing *The Indemnity*'s reactor and engines so Maya can jump. **The *Assiduous* has an EW package and is actively jamming this band.** As the Star Destroyer closes range each round, the override roll gets harder:
  • Round 1–2: Tech (Wits) + Sensors vs Resist 3 (Masterful frees engines, Legendary frees engines + shields).
  • Round 3: Resist 4 — Masterful only.
  • Round 4: Resist 5 — Legendary only.
  • Round 5: Lane closes. The *Assiduous* is in optimum jam range; the override cannot punch through.
On any tier of success, Maya is informed in real time and stops her hard-line work — the remote override means she can simply jump out. Tell the Operator player they are racing the *Assiduous*'s EW envelope, not the Hauler.

**[OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK / NO WAFER.]** The Operator lane is closed from Round 1. The crew never recovered 137.12. Skip the lane entirely and tell the Operator that the slave-circuit band is a wall of *Assiduous* white-noise — there is no remote path. Maya is alone on this.

=== MAYA'S HARD-LINE OVERRIDE (UNJAMMABLE) ===
Maya is at the *Indemnity*'s bridge override panel. She is rewiring the slave-circuit handshake by hand. **This path cannot be jammed by the *Assiduous*** — she is physically inside the firmware. Track her work as a **5-progress dramatic clock** that ticks up by 1 each round automatically (she gets one full round at the panel each comm beat). PCs can spend their own actions to push her clock by sending her real-time tactical information (Tech/Wits Resist 4 = +1 progress) or by suppressing the bridge-internal counter-firmware (Tech/Wits Resist 4 = +1 progress; Legendary = +2). At 5 progress she frees engines and shields; she punches the hyperdrive on the next initiative slot.

=== THE GAS HAULER (THE OBJECT OF VIOLENCE) ===
Scale-3 Starship, Hull as the GM prefers (suggested: 4 system tracks, drive section is the kill shot). The Hauler is unmanned and on rails — it does not fight back. Destroying its drive section before Round 5 cancels the impact. Crippling its handling reduces velocity enough to push the impact to Round 6 (+1 round to all other clocks). The TIE wing screens it; the wing must be punched through, tractored aside, or outflanked.

=== THREE OUTCOMES ===
1. **Hauler destroyed OR Maya frees the engines before Round 5 expires.** *The Indemnity* lights her drives. Maya, breathless: "We have gained control. Thank you." She jumps to the Takodana fallback rendezvous on the next initiative slot. The crew jumps after her. Adv3 P3 S6 (The Choice) fires with Maya alive and on the lake apron.
2. **Round 5 ends with neither lane resolved.** The Hauler impacts. *The Indemnity* breaks apart, Maya dies, the slaves die, the crew is in the blast envelope. **Total party kill is on the table** — the GM should make survival a final desperate roll (Pilot Reflex Resist 5 to clear the debris field; failure = ship dies; pass = ship limps out crippled, party survives broken).
3. **Crew abandons mid-fight (Varth's preferred outcome).** Set coordinates, jump on Round 1 or 2. Maya dies. The Indemnity dies. The TIEs let you go. Adv3 P3 S6 (The Choice) fires with Maya gone — use the bible's 'Maya's survival is optional' track.

=== THE VARTH-MASK-CRACKED MOMENT ===
If a PC is in real mechanical danger (one Trauma from incapacitation, ship one impairment from Disabled, etc.), Varth breaks character on the Banshee comm — drops the operational voice, tries the PC's actual NAME for the first time in the campaign (the 'Nicknames' bible canon — see Varth's section): 'Pilot — *<Name>* — pull off, NOW.' He then spends the *Banshee*'s next initiative slot to cover the endangered PC: a free Evade reaction donated to that PC's ship for one round. He says nothing about it afterward. He does not do this for Maya. (This is the moment most likely to make the players actively suspect what Varth is.)

=== OUTCOME A vs B FLAVOR — quick reference ===
[CANONICAL — fires regardless of Final Table flavor.] Imperial cleanup is gated on Varga's death (adv3-p3-s1 through s4), not the wafer. As long as Varga died in the hangar, the Hauler is burning toward *The Indemnity*. Run as written.
[FLAVOR — Switch's Dirty Money in play.] No wafer. Operator lane closed from Round 1. Maya's hard-line override is the only path. Her line about the slave circuits being locked still lands — the locks are on the ship, not on the comm code. Cut or reskin the 'where is that backup code' beat to 'where is that override sequence?' (and Varth answers truthfully: there is none, you are on your own).

=== STARSHIP-COMBAT BUTTON ===
The dashboard exposes a 'Begin Skirmish' tile (keyed on this scene's `starshipCombat: { enabled: true, status: 'scaffolded' }` flag). The button is **intentionally unwired** — clicking it shows a notice that combat logic is not yet wired and the GM should run this scene as the narrative scaffold above. Statblocks for the four PC-side ships are deliberately deferred; the table fills them in to taste.

scenes.title: The Choice
scenes.subtitle: End of Act I
scenes.readAloud:
The Tibanna Gas Hauler explodes in a massive fireball just meters from the slave ship. Maya's voice cuts through the static, shaking with relief: "Slave circuits fried. I have helm control. Jumping to Takodana."

The Assiduous opens fire with turbolasers. Green bolts flash past your cockpit. Varth screams from the Banshee:

"We overstayed our welcome! PUNCH IT!"

The stars stretch into lines and you're gone.

You drop out of hyperspace over Takodana. Green forests and silver lakes fill the viewport below — and hanging in low orbit, engines dark, is the Indemnity. A massive Imperial bulk transport, its hull scarred and ugly, cargo bays built for three hundred bodies in chains. The slave circuits are dark. The running lights are on.

Maya got here first.
scenes.gmNotes:
The aftermath of Act I. The crew arrives at Takodana to find the Indemnity already in orbit — Maya jumped here ahead of them. The bulk transport is too large to land; it sits in low orbit while Maya shuttles freed slaves down to Maz Kanata's castle. Denia is already planetside — she's been recovering at Maz's since the end of Adventure 2. The Banshee is docked at the castle.

When the crew lands at Maz's castle, Maya is waiting. She walks straight to Varth and punches him in the jaw. He takes it. 'She made her choice. And you made yours.' Varth doesn't apologize — he never does.

Rewards: The Glorious Chariot, Z-95 fighters, tournament winnings, Varga's assets, Project Leviathan files. Varth unlocks the encrypted account and pays the crew their cut.

Varth's pivot: 'This data points to a massive construction project in the Unknown Regions. If you want to know what the Empire is really building, we have to go off the map.' He looks at Denia: 'How did the Jedi navigate this part of space?' Denia suggests the Ebon Spire on the forest moon of Endor. Varth nods like he's hearing it for the first time.

This concludes Act I and sets up the campaign's second act. Takodana — Maz's castle — is the crew's home base.

[OUTCOME B — VARTH RECOLOR.] Under Outcome B (Dirty Money fork won at adv3-p2-s4), Maya never went to the Indemnity on her own — because the Indemnity lead never surfaced. Varth's deception in this scene is recolored: he is not concealing what he allowed to happen to Maya at the slave transport, he is concealing the simpler, drier truth that he was prepared to let it happen if the lead had materialized. Maya is alive and on the Banshee. The moral weight of this scene shifts from "what Varth let Maya die for" to "what Varth was willing to let her die for." Same fracture, different evidence in hand.

=== ANTIQUITIES-REP CAMEO — ACT-2 SEED (GM ONLY) ===
During the payout celebration at Maz's, an unnamed antiquities-dealer's representative — a quiet woman in a plain dark coat — approaches one PC, delivers the single line of dialogue scripted in the NPC entry below, leaves a small embossed card with only a Coruscant comm code, and exits. She does not give a name. She does not wait for an answer. The comm code on the card will not connect for several months. This is the first whisper of the Axis-network arc that pays off in Adv5+ — do not name her, her patron, or the network here. One line, one prop, no mechanical impact in Adv3.
